lead_en: Turning points that changed how many people lived, one question at a time: a 3D history globe, a timeline that shows what was happening in other places at the same moment, and an honest look at how we know.
lead_zh: 改變了很多人生活的轉折點，一課問一個問題：3D 歷史地球儀、看得到「同一個時間，別的地方在做什麼」的時間軸，還有老實交代「我們怎麼知道」。

intro.en: World history is too big to finish. This series does not try. It picks turning points, the moments that changed how many people lived, and asks one question in each lesson: Why did people start farming? What traveled along the Silk Road? Why did ships sail around the world?
intro.zh: 世界歷史太大，講不完。這個系列不打算講完，只挑轉折點——那些改變了很多人生活的時刻——每一課問一個問題：人為什麼開始種田？絲路上走的是什麼？船為什麼要繞地球一圈？

intro.en: Every lesson has a parallel timeline with seven lanes, so you can see what was happening in other parts of the world at the same time, and four cards that never change: How do we know? Different accounts. History English. And Taiwan at that time, which ties the wider world back to this island.
intro.zh: 每一課都有一條分成七條線的平行時間軸，讓你看到同一個時間世界其他地方在做什麼；還有四張固定的卡：「我們怎麼知道？」「不同的說法」「歷史英語」，以及把世界接回這座島的「那時候的台灣」。

intro.en: The lessons are written in English with a Chinese translation beside every paragraph, for upper elementary and junior high students, for teachers of bilingual classes, and for anyone who is curious. The series stops around the year 2000; what came after is still too close to see clearly.
intro.zh: 課文用英文寫，每一段旁邊都有中文翻譯，給國小高年級到國中的學生、雙語課的老師，以及所有好奇的人。全系列寫到西元 2000 年前後為止；之後的事離現在太近，還看不清楚。

rules_head.eyebrow: How This Series Is Written · 這個系列怎麼寫
rules_head.lead_en: History is easy to bend. These are the rules every lesson follows, so that you can check us against them.
rules_head.lead_zh: 歷史很容易被寫歪。下面是每一課都遵守的約定，寫出來，讓你可以拿它來檢查我們。

rules.en: Facts with sources, and no side taken
rules.zh: 只寫查得到出處的事實，不替立場說話
rules.body_en: Each lesson lists where its facts come from. Where historians disagree, the accounts are set side by side and the lesson does not pick a winner.
rules.body_zh: 每一課都列出事實的出處。歷史學家看法不同的地方，把說法並列，不替誰下結論。

rules.body_en: Africa, Asia, the Americas, Europe, and Oceania all have lessons of their own. No people are called advanced or backward; each lesson asks how people answered the place and the problems they had.
rules.body_zh: 非洲、亞洲、美洲、歐洲、大洋洲都有自己的課。不說哪一群人「先進」或「落後」，只問每個地方的人怎麼回應自己的環境和難題。

rules.body_en: The lessons keep three things apart: what believers hold, what tradition says, and what written and archaeological sources show. Every faith is treated with respect, and none is compared with another.
rules.body_zh: 課文把三件事分開：信徒相信的、傳統上說的、文獻與考古顯示的。每一種信仰都受到尊重，彼此不比較高下。

rules.body_en: Slavery, colonial rule, world wars, and genocide are part of the story. The lessons say what happened, why it matters, and how people remember it, without graphic detail. Where estimates differ, they are shown together with their sources.
rules.body_zh: 奴隸貿易、殖民統治、世界大戰、大屠殺都是歷史的一部分。課文講發生了什麼、為什麼重要、後來的人怎麼記得，不描寫血腥細節；數字有不同估計時，連同出處一起並列。

rules.en: Maps are approximate, and say so
rules.zh: 地圖只畫大約，而且會說明
rules.body_en: Old empires and old routes had no sharp edges. The globe shows rough extents with their dates and sources, and never draws today's borders onto the past.
rules.body_zh: 古代的帝國和路線沒有清楚的邊。地球儀上只畫大約的範圍，標明年代與依據，不把今天的國界畫進古代。

rules.body_en: New finds overturn old dates. The lessons say “about,” “researchers estimate,” and “the evidence so far” because that is the honest state of what is known.
rules.body_zh: 新的發現會推翻舊的年代。課文寫「大約」「研究者估計」「目前的證據顯示」，因為這才是我們所知道的真實狀態。

units.blurb_en: How people spread across the world, why they began to farm, why they invented writing, and why the first cities grew beside rivers.
units.blurb_zh: 人類怎麼走到世界各地、為什麼開始種田、為什麼發明文字，以及最早的城市為什麼都在河邊。

lessons.title: How Did Humans Spread Across the World?
lessons.title_zh: 人類怎麼走到世界各地？
lessons.blurb_en: Pull a time slider and watch people spread from Africa across a 3D globe. Lower the sea to ice-age levels to find the land bridges, click the places where the evidence was found, and see why every date in this story begins with “about.”
lessons.blurb_zh: 拉動時間滑桿，在 3D 地球儀上看人類從非洲走到世界各地。把海面降到冰河時期的高度找出陸橋，點一點發現證據的地方，看看為什麼這個故事裡的每一個年代前面都有「大約」。
lessons.big_idea_en: Everyone alive today descends mainly from people who lived in Africa long ago. Over tens of thousands of years, their descendants spread to every continent except Antarctica. We know this from fossils, stone tools, and DNA, and new discoveries keep changing the details.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 現在所有的人，主要都是很久以前住在非洲的人的後代。他們的子孫花了幾萬年，走到了南極洲以外的每一洲。我們是靠化石、石器和 DNA 知道的——而且新的發現還在不斷修改這個故事的細節。

lab.title_en: The History Globe: Out of Africa, Across the World
lab.title_zh: 歷史地球儀：從非洲出發，走到世界各地
lab.how_en: Press Play, or pull the time slider, and watch the routes grow out of Africa. A label appears when the evidence says people may have reached a region, with a range of years, never a single number. Turn on “Ice-age sea level” to see the sea drop and land bridges appear, then look for the places where people still had to cross open water. Click a white dot to see what was found there and how its age is known. The globe shows only land, sea, and routes: no borders and no country names, because none of them existed yet.
lab.how_zh: 按「播放」或拉動時間滑桿，看路線從非洲長出去。證據顯示人可能已經到達某個地區的時候，那裡會出現標示——寫的是一段年代範圍，不是單一個數字。打開「冰河時期的海平面」，看海水退下去、陸橋露出來，再找找哪些地方還是得渡海。點白色的圓點，看那裡發現了什麼、年代是怎麼知道的。地球儀上只畫陸地、海洋和路線：沒有國界，也沒有國名，因為那時候這些都還不存在。
lab.ice_note_en: This layer shows the lowest sea level of the last ice age, about 21,000 years ago. Estimates of how far the sea fell differ from study to study, from about 125 to about 134 meters below today's level. Before and after that low point the sea stood higher, so less land was exposed. The sand-colored land is a sketch made by lowering today's seafloor by 120 meters, a little less than those estimates; real coastlines differed in detail. White shows the northern ice sheets at their greatest extent.
lab.ice_note_zh: 這一層畫的是上一次冰河時期海平面最低的時候，大約 2.1 萬年前。海面到底降了多少，不同研究的估計不一樣，從比現在低約 125 公尺到約 134 公尺都有。在這個最低點之前和之後，海面都比較高，露出來的陸地也比較少。沙色的陸地是把今天的海底地形往下「放水」120 公尺畫出來的示意（比上面的估計少一點），真正的海岸線在細節上不一樣。白色是北半球冰層最大的時候的範圍。

legend.en: Land today (outline only; no borders are drawn)
legend.zh: 今天的陸地（只有外形，不畫國界）

legend.en: Land that was dry when the ice-age sea was lowest (a sketch)
legend.zh: 冰河時期海面最低時露出的陸地（示意）

legend.en: Northern ice sheets at their greatest extent
legend.zh: 北半球冰層最大時的範圍

legend.en: A rough route: direction and order only, not a real path
legend.zh: 大略的路線：只表示方向與先後，不是真的走過的路

legend.en: Dashed: an earlier move, or a route still debated
legend.zh: 虛線：較早的一次移動，或還在爭論的路線

legend.en: Blue dashes: a stretch that had to be crossed by sea
legend.zh: 藍色虛線：一定要渡海的那一段

legend.en: Purple: later voyages across the Pacific
legend.zh: 紫色：後來橫越太平洋的航行

legend.en: A discovery site you can click
legend.zh: 可以點的發現地點

lab.scale_en: The routes are a teaching sketch. They show the general direction and order in which people spread, drawn to arrive near the middle of each estimated range. Nobody knows the actual paths, and each line stands for thousands of years of small moves by many groups. The dashed line from Taiwan into the Pacific follows one widely held view, based on comparing languages, that the Austronesian-speaking voyagers set out from Taiwan about 5,000 years ago; another view has them spreading more slowly from the islands farther south. The time slider is stretched: each step back is a bigger jump in years.
lab.scale_zh: 路線是教學用的示意，只表示人類擴散的大致方向與先後，抵達的時間畫在每一段估計範圍的中間附近。真正走過的路沒有人知道；每一條線代表的是許多群人、幾千年裡一小步一小步的移動。從台灣伸向太平洋的那條虛線，依據的是一種很多人接受的看法（比較語言得出的）：說南島語的航海者大約 5,000 年前從台灣出發；另一種看法則認為他們是從更南邊的島嶼慢慢擴散開來的。時間滑桿是拉伸過的：越往回，每一格跳過的年數越多。
lab.credit_html: Land outlines: Natural Earth, 1:50m Land, version 5.1.2, public domain (naturalearthdata.com). Ice-age land: today's seafloor from NOAA ETOPO1 (Amante and Eakins 2009, public domain) lowered by 120 m; no correction for later uplift, sinking, or sediment. Ice sheets: simplified from the Last Glacial Maximum reconstruction of Batchelor et al. (2019), Nature Communications 10: 3713, CC BY 4.0; Northern Hemisphere only. Routes and ranges: drawn for this lesson from the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 陸地外形：Natural Earth 1:50m Land 5.1.2 版，公有領域。冰河時期的陸地：把 NOAA ETOPO1 的今日海底地形（Amante 與 Eakins 2009，公有領域）往下放水 120 公尺，沒有修正後來的地殼升降與沉積。冰層：依 Batchelor 等人（2019，《Nature Communications》10: 3713，CC BY 4.0）的末次冰盛期重建簡化，只有北半球。路線與年代範圍：依本頁最下面列出的資料，為這一課繪製。

bridges.zh: 白令陸橋：亞洲和北美洲相連

sites.what_en: Skull pieces, jaws, and teeth from at least five people, found with stone tools and the bones of animals they hunted.
sites.what_zh: 至少五個人的頭骨碎片、下顎和牙齒，旁邊還有石器和他們獵來的動物骨頭。
sites.when_en: About 300,000 years ago (the published date is about 315,000, give or take 34,000).
sites.when_zh: 大約 30 萬年前（發表的年代是大約 31.5 萬年前，誤差正負 3.4 萬年）。
sites.dated_en: Some of the flint tools had been heated in fires. Thermoluminescence dating measures how long ago a stone was last heated.
sites.dated_zh: 有些燧石石器被火燒過。熱螢光定年法可以量出一塊石頭上一次被加熱是多久以前。
sites.note_en: Announced in 2017. Before that, the oldest known fossils of our species were about 195,000 years old. The researchers describe these people as an early stage of our species: their faces were like ours, but their braincases were longer and lower.
sites.note_zh: 2017 年發表。在這之前，已知最古老的智人化石大約是 19.5 萬年前的。研究者形容這些人是智人的早期階段：臉和我們很像，但腦殼比較長、比較低。

sites.what_en: A partial skeleton known as Omo I, found in 1967, with a tall, rounded braincase and a chin like ours.
sites.what_zh: 一具不完整的骨骸，稱為「奧莫一號」，1967 年發現；頭骨圓、有下巴，和我們很像。
sites.when_en: At least about 233,000 years ago, by a 2022 study; an earlier study said about 195,000.
sites.when_zh: 2022 年的研究認為至少大約 23.3 萬年前；較早的研究說大約 19.5 萬年前。
sites.dated_en: The bones lay below a layer of volcanic ash. Scientists dated the eruption that made the ash, so the bones must be older than that.
sites.dated_zh: 骨骸埋在一層火山灰下面。科學家定出那次火山噴發的年代，所以骨骸一定比它更早。

sites.where_en: West Asia, near the Mediterranean coast
sites.what_en: Part of an upper jaw with several teeth, found with stone tools.
sites.what_zh: 一塊帶著幾顆牙齒的上顎，旁邊有石器。
sites.when_en: About 194,000 to 177,000 years ago according to the team that found it (2018). Other researchers argue the dating only shows it is at least 60,000 to 70,000 years old.
sites.when_zh: 發現它的團隊（2018）說大約 19.4 萬到 17.7 萬年前；也有研究者認為，這些定年只能證明它至少有 6 萬到 7 萬年。
sites.dated_en: Several methods were used on the tooth, on the crust stuck to the bone, and on burned flint nearby (uranium-series, electron spin resonance, and thermoluminescence).
sites.dated_zh: 對牙齒、黏在骨頭上的結殼和旁邊燒過的燧石用了好幾種方法（鈾系定年、電子自旋共振、熱螢光）。
sites.note_en: At two other caves in the same region, Skhul and Qafzeh, fossils of our species are dated to about 120,000 to 90,000 years ago. Those dates have long been accepted.
sites.note_zh: 同一個地區的另外兩處洞穴（斯虎爾和卡夫澤）出土的智人化石，年代大約是 12 萬到 9 萬年前。這個年代長久以來都被接受。

sites.what_en: Stone tools, grinding stones, and pieces of ground ochre (a red and yellow pigment), buried in the floor of a rock shelter.
sites.what_zh: 石器、磨石，以及磨過的赭石（紅色和黃色的顏料），埋在一處岩棚的地層裡。
sites.when_en: About 65,000 years ago by a 2017 study. Other researchers argue that the tools may have sunk through the sand into older layers, and that people arrived no more than about 50,000 years ago.
sites.when_zh: 2017 年的研究說大約 6.5 萬年前。也有研究者認為石器可能在沙層裡往下沉到了更老的地層，人類抵達的時間不會早於大約 5 萬年前。
sites.dated_en: Optically stimulated luminescence measures when grains of sand around the tools last saw sunlight.
sites.dated_zh: 光螢光定年法可以量出石器周圍的沙粒上一次曬到太陽是多久以前。
sites.note_en: No human bones this old have been found in Australia. Here the tools are the evidence.
sites.note_zh: 澳洲還沒有發現這麼古老的人骨。在這裡，證據是石器。

sites.what_en: The remains of a woman and a man, laid to rest with ceremony beside a lake that is now dry. They are the oldest human remains found in Australia so far.
sites.what_zh: 一位女性和一位男性的遺骸，被人用儀式安葬在一座現在已經乾掉的湖邊。這是澳洲目前發現最古老的人類遺骸。
sites.when_zh: 大約 4.2 萬到 4 萬年前。
sites.dated_en: Luminescence dating of the sand in which they were buried.
sites.dated_zh: 對埋葬他們的沙層做螢光定年。
sites.note_en: The Aboriginal peoples of the region regard them as ancestors, and the remains have been returned to their care.
sites.note_zh: 當地的原住民族把他們視為祖先，遺骸已經交還給他們照顧。

sites.what_en: A tooth and small pieces of bone, with stone tools and pendants made from the teeth of cave bears.
sites.what_zh: 一顆牙齒和一些碎骨，還有石器，以及用洞熊牙齒做的墜飾。
sites.dated_en: Radiocarbon dating of the bones. The pieces were too small to recognize by shape, so they were identified as human from their proteins and DNA.
sites.dated_zh: 對骨頭做放射性碳定年。碎骨太小，從形狀認不出來，是靠裡面的蛋白質和 DNA 才確定是人的。

sites.what_en: Part of a skeleton: a jaw, leg bones, and other pieces from one person.
sites.what_zh: 一個人的部分骨骸：下顎、腿骨和其他骨頭。
sites.dated_en: Radiocarbon dating of the bone itself.
sites.dated_zh: 直接對骨頭做放射性碳定年。
sites.note_en: DNA from the leg bone shows this person was related to the ancestors of many present-day Asians and Native Americans.
sites.note_zh: 從腿骨取得的 DNA 顯示，這個人和許多現代亞洲人、美洲原住民的祖先有親緣關係。

sites.what_en: Stone tools chipped from pebbles, with traces of fire, in sea caves high above today's shore. Archaeologists call the way of life of the people who made them the Changbin Culture.
sites.what_zh: 用礫石打出來的石器和用火的痕跡，出土在高出今日海面的海蝕洞裡。考古學家把製作這些石器的人的生活方式稱為長濱文化。
sites.when_en: The oldest layers are about 30,000 years old.
sites.when_zh: 最古老的地層大約是 3 萬年前。
sites.dated_en: Radiocarbon dating of charcoal from the layers where the tools lay.
sites.dated_zh: 對石器所在地層裡的木炭做放射性碳定年。
sites.note_en: This is the oldest prehistoric culture known in Taiwan so far.
sites.note_zh: 這是台灣目前所知最古老的史前文化。

sites.what_en: Human footprints, many of them left by teenagers and children, pressed into the mud of an ancient lakeshore.
sites.what_zh: 人的腳印，其中很多是青少年和小孩留下的，踩在古代湖岸的泥地上。
sites.when_zh: 大約 2.3 萬到 2.1 萬年前。
sites.dated_en: Radiocarbon dating of seeds in the layers above and below the footprints (2021), then checked with pollen and with luminescence dating (2023).
sites.dated_zh: 對腳印上下地層裡的種子做放射性碳定年（2021），之後又用花粉和螢光定年再檢查一次（2023）。
sites.note_en: If the dates are right, people were in the Americas thousands of years earlier than was long thought. Some researchers still question the dates.
sites.note_zh: 如果年代沒錯，人類到美洲的時間比長久以來認為的早了好幾千年。仍有研究者對這個年代有疑問。

sites.what_en: A campsite buried under a peat bog, which kept things that usually rot: the wooden base of a long tent-like shelter, hearths, stone tools, seaweed, and dozens of kinds of plants used as food and medicine.
sites.what_zh: 一處埋在泥炭沼澤底下的營地，保存了平常會爛掉的東西：一座長形帳篷式住屋的木頭基座、火塘、石器、海藻，以及幾十種當作食物和藥的植物。
sites.when_en: About 14,500 years ago, according to the team that excavated it. A study published in 2026 argues that the site is only about 8,000 to 4,000 years old; the excavators and other researchers reject that. The question is open.
sites.when_zh: 發掘它的團隊說大約 1.45 萬年前。2026 年發表的一項研究主張這處遺址只有大約 8,000 到 4,000 年；發掘團隊和其他研究者不接受這個說法。這個問題還沒有定論。
sites.dated_en: Radiocarbon dating of seaweed, wood, and other remains from the camp, with luminescence dating added later. The 2026 study re-dated the layers of earth around the site.
sites.dated_zh: 對營地裡的海藻、木頭和其他遺留做放射性碳定年，後來又加上螢光定年。2026 年的研究則是重新替遺址周圍的地層定年。
sites.note_en: For decades this site was the best-known evidence that people reached South America before 13,000 years ago. It lies about as far from the Bering Strait as one can go in the Americas, so if the older date holds, people must have entered the continents well before it.
sites.note_zh: 幾十年來，這處遺址是「人類在 1.3 萬年前以前就到了南美洲」最有名的證據。這裡幾乎是美洲離白令海峽最遠的地方，所以如果較早的年代成立，人類進入美洲的時間一定比它更早。

paras: Look around your classroom. Every person in it, and every person on Earth, belongs to one species, Homo sapiens. The oldest fossils of our species found so far come from Africa, and they are about 300,000 years old. For most of the time since then, almost all of our ancestors lived in Africa. Today people live on every continent except Antarctica, on high mountains and on small islands far out in the ocean. How did we get everywhere?

Nobody set out to travel the world. A group might move a short way to follow the animals it hunted, to find fresh water, or to make room for a growing family. Their grandchildren moved a little farther. Over thousands of years, these small steps added up to whole continents. Some groups left Africa very early, perhaps more than 100,000 years ago. But researchers think that most people outside Africa today descend mainly from groups that left later, roughly 70,000 to 50,000 years ago.

The world those people walked into was colder than ours. During the last ice age, so much water was frozen into huge ice sheets that the sea stood far lower than it does today: more than 120 meters lower at its lowest point, about 21,000 years ago. Shallow seas became dry land. Asia and North America were joined by a wide plain called Beringia. Australia and New Guinea were one landmass. Taiwan was part of the Asian mainland.

Land bridges did not reach everywhere. Between Southeast Asia and Australia the water stayed deep, so the first people to reach Australia must have crossed open sea, at least 50,000 years ago and perhaps 65,000 years ago. People were living in Europe by about 45,000 years ago. Most researchers think they had reached the Americas by about 15,000 years ago, and footprints found in North America may be 23,000 years old. The last large lands to be settled were islands deep in the Pacific. Voyagers reached New Zealand only about 750 years ago.

How can anyone know what happened before writing existed? Researchers use three kinds of evidence. Fossils show what people's bodies were like. Stone tools show where people lived, even in places where no bones have survived. DNA, taken from living people and sometimes from very old bones, shows how groups are related. None of the three gives an exact date. That is why this lesson keeps saying “about,” and why it gives a range instead of a single number.

Our species was not alone. Other kinds of humans, such as the Neanderthals, were already living in Europe and Asia. They were not our ancestors in a straight line, but close relatives, and DNA shows that the two groups sometimes had children together. The story is still being rewritten. Until 2017, the oldest known fossils of our species were about 195,000 years old; then a find in Morocco pushed that back by 100,000 years. The next discovery may change this lesson too.
paras_zh: 看看你的教室。教室裡的每一個人，還有地球上的每一個人，都屬於同一個物種：智人。目前找到最古老的智人化石來自非洲，大約是 30 萬年前的。從那時候起的大部分時間，我們的祖先幾乎都住在非洲。今天，除了南極洲以外的每一洲都有人住，高山上有，大洋深處的小島上也有。我們是怎麼走到每個地方的？
沒有人是為了「走遍世界」而出發的。一群人也許只是為了追著獵物、找乾淨的水，或是家族人口變多了需要空間，而搬到不遠的地方。他們的孫子又搬得更遠一點。幾千年下來，這些小小的腳步加起來，就跨過了一整塊大陸。有些人很早就離開了非洲，也許是 10 萬年以前。不過研究者認為，今天住在非洲以外的人，主要是比較晚離開的那些人的後代，他們大約在 7 萬到 5 萬年前離開。
那些人走進的世界比現在冷。在上一次冰河時期，很多水結成了巨大的冰層，海面比今天低得多：最低的時候大約在 2.1 萬年前，比現在低了 120 公尺以上。淺海變成了陸地。亞洲和北美洲之間有一片寬廣的平原相連，叫做白令陸橋。澳洲和新幾內亞是同一塊陸地。台灣和亞洲大陸連在一起。
但陸橋並沒有通到每一個地方。東南亞和澳洲之間的海一直很深，所以最早到達澳洲的人一定渡過了海——至少在 5 萬年前，也可能早到 6.5 萬年前。大約 4.5 萬年前，歐洲已經有人居住。多數研究者認為，人類大約在 1.5 萬年前已經到了美洲，而在北美洲發現的腳印可能有 2.3 萬年那麼久。最後才有人定居的大片陸地，是太平洋深處的島嶼。航海者大約 750 年前才抵達紐西蘭。
沒有文字的時代發生的事，怎麼可能知道？研究者靠三種證據。化石讓我們看到人的身體長什麼樣子。石器告訴我們哪裡有人住過，就算那裡沒有留下任何骨頭。DNA（取自現代人，有時也取自很古老的骨頭）告訴我們不同的人群之間有什麼親緣關係。這三種證據都給不出精確的年代。所以這一課一直在說「大約」，而且給的是一段範圍，不是單一個數字。
我們這個物種並不孤單。那時候歐洲和亞洲已經住著別種人類，例如尼安德塔人。他們不是我們「一直線往上」的祖先，而是關係很近的親戚；DNA 顯示，兩群人有時候會生下共同的孩子。這個故事到現在還在被改寫。在 2017 年以前，已知最古老的智人化石大約是 19.5 萬年前的；後來摩洛哥的一項發現，把這個年代往前推了 10 萬年。下一個發現，也可能改寫這一課。
questions: The lesson says that nobody “set out to travel the world.” How, then, did people end up on almost every continent?
Why did the first people to reach Australia need boats or rafts, even though the sea was much lower in the ice age?
Why does this lesson give a range of years, such as “65,000 to 50,000 years ago,” instead of one exact date?
answers: By many small moves over a very long time. A group moved a short distance to follow animals, find water, or make room for more people; later generations moved a little farther. Over thousands of years, those short moves added up to great distances.

The land bridges did not reach all the way. The water between Southeast Asia and Australia was too deep to become dry land, even when the sea was at its lowest. So people must have crossed open sea to get there.

Because the evidence cannot give an exact date. Every dating method has a margin of error, different sites and different studies give different results, and new finds keep changing the picture. A range is the honest way to say what is known.

vocab.ex: Your grandmother's grandmother is one of your ancestors.
vocab.exzh: 你阿嬤的阿嬤是你的祖先之一。

vocab.ex: The fossil was a jawbone with three teeth still in it.
vocab.exzh: 那件化石是一塊下顎骨，上面還留著三顆牙齒。

vocab.ex: She found a stone tool with a sharp edge for cutting.
vocab.exzh: 她找到一件石器，有一道可以用來切東西的鋒利邊緣。

vocab.ex: DNA carries the instructions that parents pass on to their children.
vocab.exzh: DNA 帶著父母傳給孩子的遺傳指令。

vocab.ex: The migration of people out of Africa took thousands of years.
vocab.exzh: 人類走出非洲的遷徙花了幾千年。

vocab.ex: During the last ice age, thick ice covered much of North America.
vocab.exzh: 上一次冰河時期，厚厚的冰蓋住了北美洲的大片土地。

vocab.ex: People and animals walked across the land bridge between the two continents.
vocab.exzh: 人和動物走過連接兩塊大陸的陸橋。

vocab.ex: The footprints are evidence that people were there.
vocab.exzh: 那些腳印是有人到過那裡的證據。

quiz.q: Where do the oldest known fossils of our species, Homo sapiens, come from?
Why was the sea so much lower during the last ice age?
options: So much water was frozen into ice sheets on land
The oceans had not formed yet
It rained much less all over the world
The Moon was farther from the Earth

quiz.q: Which of these did people have to reach by crossing open sea, even when the sea was at its lowest?
Which kind of evidence shows that the ancestors of living people sometimes had children with Neanderthals?
Why does this lesson say “about 45,000 years ago” and not give an exact year?
options: Dating methods have a margin of error, and new finds can change the answer
Researchers have not tried to measure it
The exact year is known but is kept secret
People in the past used a different calendar

guide.eyebrow: How to Read This Series · 這個系列怎麼讀
guide.en: Three things to know before Lesson 2
guide.zh: 讀第二課之前，先知道三件事
guide.lead_en: Every lesson in World History uses the same three tools. This first lesson is the place to learn them.
guide.lead_zh: 世界歷史的每一課都會用到這三樣工具。第一課先把它們學起來。

cards.body_en: This series counts years with BCE (Before the Common Era) and CE (Common Era). They are the same numbers as BC and AD: 500 BCE is 500 BC, and 2000 CE is AD 2000. BCE years count backward, so 3000 BCE is earlier than 500 BCE. There is no year zero: the year after 1 BCE is 1 CE. For things that happened tens of thousands of years ago, the lessons simply say “about 50,000 years ago.”
cards.body_zh: 這個系列用 BCE（西元前）和 CE（西元）來算年代。它們和 BC、AD 是同一套數字：500 BCE 就是 500 BC，2000 CE 就是 AD 2000。西元前的年份是倒著數的，所以西元前 3000 年比西元前 500 年更早。沒有「0 年」：西元前 1 年的下一年就是西元 1 年。至於幾萬年前的事，課文直接說「大約 5 萬年前」。

cards.body_en: Each lesson has a timeline with seven lanes: Africa, West Asia, Europe, South Asia, East Asia, Oceania, and the Americas. Read across a lane to follow one region through time. Read down to see what was happening in other regions at the same moment. The seven lanes are only a convenience. Central and Southeast Asia are placed on the nearest lane, every lane holds many different peoples, and the regions were never sealed off from one another.
cards.body_zh: 每一課都有一條分成七條線的時間軸：非洲、西亞、歐洲、南亞、東亞、大洋洲、美洲。橫著讀，是跟著一個區域走過時間；直著讀，是看同一個時刻別的區域在做什麼。分成七條線只是為了方便：中亞和東南亞的事放在最近的那一條；每一條線裡面都有很多不同的人群；各個區域之間也從來沒有隔絕過。

cards.zh: 為什麼會有「不同的說法」
cards.body_en: The past is gone, and only traces are left: bones, tools, buildings, and, for later times, writing. The traces are incomplete, and careful people can read them in different ways. Sometimes a new find settles a question, and sometimes it opens one. So every lesson has a card called “Different Accounts.” It sets the views side by side with their sources and does not pick a winner. Being unsure is not a weakness in history. Pretending to be sure is.
cards.body_zh: 過去已經過去了，留下來的只有痕跡：骨頭、工具、建築，以及比較晚的時代才有的文字。這些痕跡並不完整，認真研究的人也可能讀出不一樣的意思。有時候一個新發現解決了一個問題，有時候反而打開了一個新問題。所以每一課都有一張「不同的說法」卡，把各種看法連同出處並列，不替誰下結論。在歷史裡，「不確定」不是缺點；假裝確定才是。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It on the Globe · 在地球儀上試試

parts.meta_zh: 30 萬年前到大約 10 萬年前
parts.text_en: For about two thirds of our species' time on Earth, the map hardly changes: people live in Africa. Watch the dashed line of an early group reach West Asia, then notice how long it is before the main routes begin.
parts.text_zh: 我們這個物種在地球上的時間裡，大約有三分之二，地圖幾乎沒有變化：人住在非洲。看一條虛線（較早離開的一群人）走到西亞，再注意主要的路線要等多久才出現。

parts.en: The sea that had to be crossed
parts.text_en: With the ice-age sea level on, mainland Asia stretches out to Java and Borneo, and Australia joins New Guinea. Between them the sea remains. The blue dashes mark where people needed boats or rafts.
parts.text_zh: 打開冰河時期的海平面，亞洲大陸一路延伸到爪哇和婆羅洲，澳洲和新幾內亞連在一起。但兩者之間還是海。藍色的虛線就是需要船或筏的地方。

parts.en: A bridge, and a wall of ice
parts.meta_zh: 大約 2.3 萬到 1.4 萬年前
parts.text_en: Beringia joins Asia to North America, but ice sheets block the way south. Two dashed routes show the two ideas researchers discuss: down the Pacific coast, or through a gap between the ice sheets that opened later.
parts.text_zh: 白令陸橋把亞洲和北美洲連了起來，但往南的路被冰層擋住。兩條虛線是研究者討論的兩種想法：沿著太平洋海岸往南，或是穿過後來才打開的、兩片冰層之間的通道。

parts.text_en: Almost at the end of the slider, purple lines cross thousands of kilometers of open Pacific. There were no land bridges here at any time. People reached these islands by sailing across the open ocean.
parts.text_zh: 滑桿快到底的時候，紫色的線跨過幾千公里的太平洋。這裡從來沒有陸橋。人是航行過大洋，才到得了這些島的。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then explore on your own. Click the white dots, and compare the same place with the ice-age sea level on and off.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著自己探索。點一點白色的圓點，再比較同一個地方在「冰河時期的海平面」打開和關掉時有什麼不同。

order.lead_en: Put these six places in order, from the one where people of our species lived earliest to the one they reached last. Use the arrows, or drag. There is no timer. The game checks your order against ranges of years, so where two ranges overlap, either order counts as right.
order.lead_zh: 把這六個地方排好順序：從我們這個物種最早住的地方，排到最晚抵達的地方。用箭頭移動，或直接拖曳。不計時。遊戲是用「年代範圍」來判定的，所以兩個範圍重疊的地方，誰排前面都算對。
order.hint_en: Earliest at the top, most recent at the bottom. Then press Check.
order.hint_zh: 最早的排最上面，最晚的排最下面，然後按「檢查」。
order.done_en: That order fits the evidence so far.
order.done_zh: 這個順序符合目前的證據。
order.open_en: Notice the pair whose ranges overlap: researchers cannot yet say which came first, so the game accepts either order.
order.open_zh: 注意範圍重疊的那一對：研究者現在還分不出誰先誰後，所以兩種排法遊戲都接受。

items.en: Africa
West Asia (early groups)
Australia and New Guinea
Europe
The Americas
New Zealand

sort.lead_en: Fossils, stone tools, and DNA each answer different questions, and some questions none of them can answer. Read each question and choose the evidence that could answer it best. There is no timer, and you can keep choosing until you get it; the game counts how many you sort correctly on the first try.
sort.lead_zh: 化石、石器、DNA 各自能回答不同的問題，也有些問題三種都回答不了。讀每一個問題，選出最能回答它的那一種證據。不計時，可以一直選到對為止；遊戲會記下你第一次就分對的題數。
sort.ask_en: Which evidence could best answer this?
sort.ask_zh: 哪一種證據最能回答這個問題？

items.en: How tall was this person, and was the skull shaped like ours?
items.zh: 這個人有多高？頭骨的形狀和我們像不像？
items.why_en: Bones and teeth show the shape and size of a body. That is how we can tell one kind of human from another.
items.why_zh: 骨頭和牙齒可以看出身體的形狀和大小。我們就是靠這個分辨不同種類的人。
items.hint_en: Think about what actually keeps the shape of a body.
items.hint_zh: 想想什麼東西真的留下了身體的形狀。

items.en: Were people living at this place, even though no bones have survived there?
items.zh: 這個地方沒有留下任何人骨，那時候有人住在這裡嗎？
items.why_en: Stone lasts far longer than bone. In many places, tools are the only sign that people were there.
items.why_zh: 石頭比骨頭耐久得多。很多地方，石器是「有人來過」唯一的痕跡。
items.hint_en: Bones rot away in most soils. What does not?
items.hint_zh: 骨頭在大多數的土壤裡會爛掉。什麼東西不會？

items.en: Did the ancestors of people alive today have children with Neanderthals?
items.zh: 今天的人的祖先，有沒有和尼安德塔人生下小孩？
items.why_en: Only DNA can show this. Small stretches of Neanderthal DNA are still found in many people today.
items.why_zh: 這只有 DNA 才看得出來。今天很多人身上還帶著一小段一小段尼安德塔人的 DNA。
items.hint_en: Family relationships are written somewhere inside every cell.
items.hint_zh: 親緣關係寫在每一個細胞裡的某個地方。

items.en: How did these people make a sharp cutting edge?
items.zh: 這些人是怎麼做出鋒利的刀刃的？
items.why_en: The chips and scars on a stone tool record each blow, so experts can work out how it was made.
items.why_zh: 石器上的每一道疤痕都記錄了一次敲打，專家可以從這些痕跡還原它是怎麼做出來的。
items.hint_en: Look at the thing that was made.
items.hint_zh: 看看被做出來的那樣東西。

items.en: Which groups of people living today are most closely related to each other?
items.zh: 今天的哪些人群，彼此的親緣關係最近？
items.why_en: Comparing the DNA of living people shows who shares more recent ancestors.
items.why_zh: 比較現代人的 DNA，可以看出誰和誰有比較近的共同祖先。
items.hint_en: You can study this without digging at all.
items.hint_zh: 這個問題不用挖土也能研究。

items.en: Had this person broken an arm years before dying, and did it heal?
items.zh: 這個人在過世的好幾年前摔斷過手臂嗎？後來有沒有長好？
items.why_en: A healed break leaves a mark on the bone, so a fossil can show that a person lived on for years after an injury.
items.why_zh: 骨折癒合會在骨頭上留下痕跡，所以化石可以告訴我們：一個人受傷以後又活了好幾年。
items.hint_en: The answer is in the body itself.
items.hint_zh: 答案就在身體上。

items.en: What language did these people speak, and what did they call themselves?
items.zh: 這些人說什麼語言？他們怎麼稱呼自己？
items.why_en: Spoken words leave no trace. The earliest known writing is a little more than 5,000 years old, so for almost all of this story we do not know a single name.
items.why_zh: 說出來的話不會留下痕跡。已知最早的文字只有五千年多一點，所以這個故事的絕大部分，我們連一個名字都不知道。
items.hint_en: Can a sound be dug up?
items.hint_zh: 聲音挖得出來嗎？

items.en: About when did two groups of people separate and stop mixing?
items.zh: 兩群人大約是什麼時候分開、不再往來的？
items.why_en: Small changes build up in DNA over time. Counting the differences between two groups gives a rough estimate of when they split.
items.why_zh: DNA 會隨著時間累積小小的改變。數一數兩群人之間的差異，可以大略估計他們是什麼時候分開的。
items.hint_en: Something that changes slowly and steadily can work like a clock.
items.hint_zh: 會緩慢而穩定地改變的東西，可以當時鐘用。

items.en: Did people carry this kind of stone here from a place far away?
items.zh: 這種石頭，是人從很遠的地方帶過來的嗎？
items.why_en: Geologists can often match a stone to the outcrop it came from. A tool found far from its source shows that people traveled or traded.
items.why_zh: 地質學家常常能認出一塊石頭來自哪一處岩層。離產地很遠的石器，表示有人帶著它走了很遠，或者和別人交換過。
items.hint_en: Stones have hometowns too.
items.hint_zh: 石頭也有故鄉。

items.en: What stories did they tell their children at night?
items.zh: 晚上他們對孩子說什麼故事？
items.why_en: No bone, stone, or gene records a story. Knowing where the evidence stops is part of doing history honestly.
items.why_zh: 骨頭、石頭、基因都記不下一個故事。知道證據到哪裡為止，是老實做歷史的一部分。
items.hint_en: Some things are simply lost.
items.hint_zh: 有些事情就是失傳了。

sort.end_en: Each kind of evidence answers some questions and is silent on others. The story of how people spread is built by fitting all three together, and by admitting what none of them can say.
sort.end_zh: 每一種證據都能回答一些問題，對另一些問題則沉默。人類怎麼走到世界各地的故事，是把三種證據拼在一起得來的——同時也要承認，有些事三種都說不出來。

timeline.en: The same story, lane by lane
timeline.zh: 同一個故事，一條線一條線看
timeline.lead_en: The bars show the estimated range for when people of our species first lived in each region. The gold band marks the time this lesson covers, which is nearly all of it. Try the button “Every year the same width,” and see how thin the last 5,300 years or so, the age of writing, really are.
timeline.lead_zh: 長條是「智人最早在這個區域生活」的估計範圍。金色的帶子標出這一課講的時間——幾乎是全部。按「每一年一樣寬」看看：最近的五千三百年左右，也就是有文字的時代，其實只有薄薄一條。
timeline.idle_en: Click a bar or a diamond to read its dates. Drag sideways to move through time.
timeline.idle_zh: 點一條長條或一個菱形，讀出它的年代。左右拖曳可以在時間裡移動。

tips.en: Read across to follow one region; read down to compare regions at the same moment.
tips.zh: 橫著讀，跟著一個區域走；直著讀，比較同一個時刻的不同區域。

tips.en: A long bar does not mean a long journey. It means the evidence leaves a wide range of possible dates.
tips.zh: 長條很長，不代表走了很久，而是代表證據留下的可能年代範圍很寬。

tips.en: A striped bar marks dates that researchers still debate.
tips.zh: 有條紋的長條，是研究者還在爭論的年代。

tips.en: The gray diamond is a signpost to a later lesson, so you can see how far away it is.
tips.zh: 灰色的菱形是後面一課的路標，讓你看看它離這裡有多遠。

events.en: Oldest known fossils of our species
events.zh: 已知最古老的智人化石
events.note_en: Jebel Irhoud, in northwest Africa: about 315,000 years old, give or take 34,000.
events.note_zh: 非洲西北部的傑貝爾依羅：大約 31.5 萬年前，誤差正負 3.4 萬年。

events.note_en: Fossils from Skhul and Qafzeh are about 120,000 to 90,000 years old. An older date from Misliya Cave is debated.
events.note_zh: 斯虎爾和卡夫澤的化石大約是 12 萬到 9 萬年前；米斯利亞洞穴更早的年代還有爭論。

events.note_en: Proto-cuneiform, the system of signs on clay tablets that grew into the earliest known writing, emerged in Mesopotamia about 3350 to 3200 BCE. From here on, some people left written records. Before this, all we have is fossils, objects, and DNA.
events.note_zh: 寫在泥板上的原始楔形文字（後來發展成已知最早的文字）大約在西元前 3350 到 3200 年出現在美索不達米亞。從這裡開始，有些人留下了文字記錄。在這之前，我們只有化石、器物和 DNA。

events.note_en: A single tooth in a French rock shelter may be about 54,000 years old. Several sites show people in Europe by 45,000 years ago.
events.note_zh: 法國一處岩棚裡的一顆牙齒可能有大約 5.4 萬年；好幾處遺址顯示 4.5 萬年前歐洲已經有人。

events.note_en: A skull bone from a cave in Laos is about 70,000 years old. A skeleton from Tianyuan Cave in northern China is about 40,000 years old.
events.note_zh: 寮國一處洞穴出土的頭骨大約是 7 萬年前的；華北田園洞的骨骸大約是 4 萬年前的。

events.note_en: Stone tools of the Changbin Culture, the oldest prehistoric culture known in Taiwan so far.
events.note_zh: 長濱文化的石器；這是台灣目前所知最古老的史前文化。

events.note_en: Reached by sea. One site is dated to about 65,000 years ago; other researchers argue for about 50,000.
events.note_zh: 渡海抵達。有一處遺址定年為大約 6.5 萬年前；也有研究者主張大約 5 萬年前。

events.note_en: From about 3,000 years ago to about 1190 to 1290 CE, when voyagers reached New Zealand.
events.note_zh: 從大約 3,000 年前，到大約西元 1190 至 1290 年航海者抵達紐西蘭。

events.note_en: By about 15,000 years ago, most researchers think. Footprints at White Sands may be 23,000 to 21,000 years old.
events.note_zh: 多數研究者認為大約 1.5 萬年前已經有人。白沙的腳印可能有 2.3 萬到 2.1 萬年。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.lead_en: Every lesson in this series has this card. For a time with no writing at all, the evidence is of three kinds, and each has limits.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 這個系列每一課都有這張卡。在完全沒有文字的時代，證據有三種，每一種都有它的限制。

items.en: Fossils
items.limit_en: Fossils are rare. Most bodies leave nothing behind, so the oldest fossil found in a place is not the first person who lived there. A fossil also does not carry its own date; the age comes from the layers around it.
items.limit_zh: 化石很稀少。大多數的遺體什麼都不會留下，所以一個地方找到的最古老化石，並不是最早住在那裡的人。化石本身也不會標示年代，年代要靠它周圍的地層來定。
items.text_en: Bones and teeth that have lasted in the ground show what a person's body was like, and they let researchers tell our species from other kinds of humans. Footprints pressed into mud are fossils too.
items.text_zh: 留在地底下的骨頭和牙齒，讓我們看到一個人的身體是什麼樣子，也讓研究者分辨智人和其他種類的人。踩在泥地上的腳印也是化石。

items.en: Stone tools
items.limit_en: A tool does not say who made it. Where several kinds of humans lived at the same time, it can be hard to know which of them left a tool behind. Tools can also shift between layers, which is one reason dates are argued over.
items.limit_zh: 石器不會說是誰做的。在好幾種人類同時生活的地方，很難知道一件石器是哪一種人留下的。石器也可能在地層之間移動，這是年代會引起爭論的原因之一。
items.text_en: Stone lasts far longer than bone, wood, or cloth. Tools, hearths, and pigments show that people were at a place, how they made things, and sometimes how far they carried their materials.
items.text_zh: 石頭比骨頭、木頭和布都耐久得多。石器、火塘和顏料告訴我們有人到過這個地方、他們怎麼製作東西，有時還看得出他們把材料帶了多遠。

items.en: DNA
items.limit_en: DNA breaks down with time, and faster in warm, wet places, so very old DNA survives mostly in cold or dry sites. Dates worked out from DNA are estimates with wide margins.
items.limit_zh: DNA 會隨著時間分解，在又熱又濕的地方分解得更快，所以非常古老的 DNA 大多只在寒冷或乾燥的遺址保存下來。用 DNA 推算出來的年代是估計值，誤差範圍很寬。
items.src: Smithsonian Human Origins: Ancient DNA and Neanderthals
items.text_en: DNA from living people, and since the 1990s from ancient bones as well, shows how groups are related, roughly when they separated, and whether they mixed. It was DNA that showed our ancestors had children with Neanderthals.
items.text_zh: 現代人的 DNA，加上 1990 年代以來從古老骨頭裡取得的 DNA，可以告訴我們人群之間的親緣關係、大約什麼時候分開，以及有沒有混在一起。我們的祖先和尼安德塔人生過孩子這件事，就是 DNA 告訴我們的。

views.en: Four questions that are still open
views.zh: 四個還沒有定論的問題
views.lead_en: This part of the human story is being revised quickly. Here are four questions on which researchers disagree. The views are set side by side; this lesson does not choose between them.
views.lead_zh: 人類故事的這一段，正被快速地修改。下面是研究者看法不一致的四個問題。各種說法並列，這一課不替誰下結論。
views.rule_en: In later lessons this card will hold harder disagreements: about empires, about beliefs, and about wars that families still remember. The rule stays the same. Views are set side by side, each with its source, and the lesson does not choose.
views.rule_zh: 後面的課裡，這張卡會放更難的分歧：關於帝國、關於信仰、關於有些家庭至今還記得的戰爭。規則不變：說法並列，各附出處，課文不替誰選邊。

items.topic_en: When did people first reach the Americas?
items.topic_zh: 人類什麼時候最早到達美洲？

sides.en: Fossil footprints at White Sands in North America were dated in 2021 to between about 23,000 and 21,000 years ago, when ice still blocked the way from the north. A second study in 2023, using two other methods, reached the same result.
sides.zh: 北美洲白沙的腳印化石，2021 年的定年結果是大約 2.3 萬到 2.1 萬年前，那時候北邊的路還被冰擋著。2023 年另一項研究用另外兩種方法，得到同樣的結果。
sides.src: Bennett et al., Science (2021); Pigati et al., Science (2023)

sides.en: Some researchers question those dates. The seeds that were dated came from a water plant, and water plants can take in old carbon from the water. The critics say this may have made the ages appear thousands of years too old.
sides.zh: 有研究者質疑這個年代。用來定年的種子來自一種水生植物，而水生植物可能從水裡吸收古老的碳。批評者說，這可能讓定出來的年代比實際的老了好幾千年。
sides.src: Madsen et al., Science (2022), technical comment

items.note_en: The Natural History Museum in London says that exactly when people arrived “is still debated.” The debate reaches the far south too: Monte Verde, a site in South America long dated to about 14,500 years ago, was re-dated by a 2026 study to only about 8,000 to 4,000 years, and its excavators reject that result. Researchers also disagree about the route: along the Pacific coast, or through a gap between the ice sheets that one study dates to about 13,800 years ago.
items.note_zh: 倫敦自然史博物館的說法是，人類到底什麼時候抵達「仍在爭論中」。爭論也延伸到最南邊：南美洲的蒙特維德遺址長久以來被定為大約 1.45 萬年前，2026 年的一項研究把它重新定年為只有大約 8,000 到 4,000 年，而發掘團隊不接受這個結果。走哪一條路也有不同看法：沿著太平洋海岸，或是穿過兩片冰層之間的通道（有研究把通道打開的時間定在大約 1.38 萬年前）。

items.topic_en: When did people reach Australia?
items.topic_zh: 人類什麼時候到達澳洲？

sides.en: Stone tools at Madjedbebe, a rock shelter in northern Australia, were dated in 2017 to about 65,000 years ago. The Australian Museum describes the site as at least 65,000 years old.
sides.zh: 澳洲北部的馬杰貝貝岩棚出土的石器，2017 年定年為大約 6.5 萬年前。澳洲博物館對這處遺址的說法是「至少 6.5 萬年」。
sides.src: Clarkson et al., Nature (2017)

sides.en: Other researchers argue that people arrived no more than about 50,000 years ago. They point out that tools can sink through sandy ground into older layers, and that DNA evidence fits the later date better.
sides.zh: 也有研究者主張人類抵達的時間不會早於大約 5 萬年前。他們指出，石器可能在沙質的地層裡往下沉到更老的地層，而 DNA 的證據也比較符合較晚的年代。
sides.src: University of Utah (2025), on Allen and O'Connell

items.note_en: Both sides agree that people have lived in Australia for something close to 50,000 years or more, and that getting there took sea crossings. The oldest human remains found there, at Lake Mungo, are about 42,000 to 40,000 years old.
items.note_zh: 兩邊都同意：人類在澳洲生活了將近 5 萬年或更久，而且要到那裡一定得渡海。在當地發現的最古老人類遺骸（蒙哥湖）大約是 4.2 萬到 4 萬年前的。

items.topic_en: How early did our species leave Africa?
items.topic_zh: 智人最早什麼時候離開非洲？

sides.en: A piece of skull from Apidima Cave in Greece was reported in 2019 as an early member of our species more than 210,000 years old. A jaw from Misliya Cave was reported in 2018 as 177,000 to 194,000 years old.
sides.zh: 希臘阿皮迪瑪洞穴的一塊頭骨，2019 年被發表為早期的智人，年代超過 21 萬年。米斯利亞洞穴的一塊上顎，2018 年發表的年代是 17.7 萬到 19.4 萬年前。
sides.src: Harvati et al., Nature (2019); Hershkovitz et al., Science (2018)

sides.en: Critics of the Misliya dating argue that it shows only a minimum age of about 60,000 to 70,000 years. The Apidima skull is incomplete, and its describers themselves note that it mixes modern and older features.
sides.zh: 批評米斯利亞定年的研究者認為，那些數據只能證明它至少有大約 6 萬到 7 萬年。阿皮迪瑪的頭骨並不完整，發表它的研究者自己也指出，它同時有現代和比較古老的特徵。
sides.src: Sharp and Paces, Science (2018), technical comment

items.note_en: Fossils about 120,000 to 90,000 years old from Skhul and Qafzeh have long been accepted as early members of our species outside Africa. The Natural History Museum notes that such early groups seem to have died out without passing on their genes; most people outside Africa today descend mainly from a later movement.
items.note_zh: 斯虎爾和卡夫澤出土、大約 12 萬到 9 萬年前的化石，長久以來被接受是非洲以外的早期智人。倫敦自然史博物館指出，這些較早離開的人似乎沒有把基因傳下來就消失了；今天非洲以外的人，主要是後來那一次移動的後代。

items.topic_en: How were we related to the Neanderthals, and why did they disappear?
items.topic_zh: 我們和尼安德塔人是什麼關係？他們為什麼消失了？

sides.en: Neanderthals were not our direct ancestors. They and our species share an earlier common ancestor, and the two groups later had children together. People with ancestry from outside Africa carry a small share of Neanderthal DNA: about 2 percent by one museum's count, 1 to 4 percent by another's.
sides.zh: 尼安德塔人不是我們的直系祖先。他們和智人有一個更早的共同祖先，後來兩群人又生下了共同的孩子。祖先來自非洲以外的人，身上帶著一小部分尼安德塔人的 DNA：一間博物館說大約 2%，另一間說 1% 到 4%。
sides.src: Smithsonian Human Origins; Natural History Museum, London

sides.en: Sources differ on when the two lines separated: at least 500,000 years ago by the Natural History Museum's account, about 800,000 by the Nobel committee's. And no one yet knows why the Neanderthals died out.
sides.zh: 兩條支系什麼時候分開，各家的數字不一樣：倫敦自然史博物館說至少 50 萬年前，諾貝爾獎委員會說大約 80 萬年前。尼安德塔人為什麼會消失，目前也還沒有人知道。
sides.src: Natural History Museum, London, “Who were the Neanderthals?”; Nobel Prize 2022 press release

items.note_en: A third group, the Denisovans, is known mostly from DNA and a handful of fossils. Some people in Oceania and Asia today carry Denisovan DNA as well. Before 2010, nobody knew the Denisovans had existed.
items.note_zh: 還有第三群人——丹尼索瓦人，我們主要是從 DNA 和屈指可數的幾件化石認識他們的。今天大洋洲和亞洲的一些人，身上也帶著丹尼索瓦人的 DNA。在 2010 年以前，還沒有人知道丹尼索瓦人存在過。

phrases.en: Eight sentences for talking about the distant past
phrases.zh: 談很久以前的事，用得到的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: Every lesson has a History English card. These eight sentences show how to talk about time and evidence honestly: how to say “about,” how to say where an idea comes from, and how to say that something is still uncertain. Listen, repeat, then make your own sentence with the words in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 每一課都有一張「歷史英語」卡。這八句示範怎麼老實地談時間和證據：怎麼說「大約」、怎麼說一個說法是從哪裡來的、怎麼說「這件事還不確定」。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用粗體的字自己造一句。

rows.en: Our species dates back about 300,000 years.
rows.html: Our species dates back about 300,000 years.
rows.zh: 我們這個物種可以追溯到大約 30 萬年前。
rows.note_en: dates back: how far into the past something goes

rows.en: People reached Australia at least 50,000 years ago.
rows.html: People reached Australia at least 50,000 years ago.
rows.zh: 人類至少在 5 萬年前就到了澳洲。
rows.note_en: at least: this much, and maybe more

rows.en: The footprints are between 21,000 and 23,000 years old.
rows.html: The footprints are between 21,000 and 23,000 years old.
rows.zh: 那些腳印的年代在 2.1 萬到 2.3 萬年之間。
rows.note_en: between … and …: giving a range

rows.en: According to the fossil evidence, the earliest members of our species lived in Africa.
rows.html: According to the fossil evidence, the earliest members of our species lived in Africa.
rows.zh: 根據化石證據，我們這個物種最早的成員住在非洲。
rows.note_en: according to: saying where an idea comes from

rows.en: Researchers estimate that the sea was more than 120 meters lower.
rows.html: Researchers estimate that the sea was more than 120 meters lower.
rows.zh: 研究者估計，當時的海面比現在低了 120 公尺以上。
rows.note_en: estimate that: a careful guess based on evidence
rows.note_zh: 根據證據做出的謹慎推估

rows.en: It is still debated when people first reached the Americas.
rows.html: It is still debated when people first reached the Americas.
rows.zh: 人類什麼時候最早到達美洲，目前仍有爭論。
rows.note_en: it is still debated: experts do not agree yet
rows.note_zh: 專家還沒有一致的看法

rows.en: New Zealand was settled long after the other large lands.
rows.html: New Zealand was settled long after the other large lands.
rows.zh: 紐西蘭有人定居的時間，比其他大片陸地晚得多。
rows.note_en: long after: much later than

rows.en: The evidence so far suggests that the first Australians arrived by sea.
rows.html: The evidence so far suggests that the first Australians arrived by sea.
rows.zh: 目前的證據顯示，最早的澳洲人是渡海來的。
rows.note_en: the evidence so far suggests: true as far as we know now

taiwan_then.eyebrow: Taiwan at That Time · 那時候的台灣
taiwan_then.en: An island that was not always an island
taiwan_then.zh: 一座不是一直都是島的島
taiwan_then.lead_en: Every lesson ends by bringing the wider world back to Taiwan. In this lesson's long span of time, Taiwan was sometimes an island and sometimes the edge of a continent.
taiwan_then.lead_zh: 每一課的最後，都會把世界接回台灣。在這一課講的漫長時間裡，台灣有時候是一座島，有時候是大陸的邊緣。
taiwan_then.intro_en: Turn on the ice-age sea level and find Taiwan on the globe. The strait is shallow, so when the sea fell, its floor became dry land and animals and people could walk across. When the ice melted, the sea came back and Taiwan became an island again.
taiwan_then.intro_zh: 打開冰河時期的海平面，在地球儀上找到台灣。台灣海峽很淺，所以海面下降的時候，海底變成了陸地，動物和人可以直接走過來。冰融化以後，海水回來，台灣又變成一座島。

facts.k_zh: 目前所知最古老的文化
facts.en: Stone tools from the Baxian Caves in Changbin, Taitung, belong to the Changbin Culture, which the National Museum of Prehistory calls the oldest prehistoric culture in Taiwan. Excavations show that its Old Stone Age layers are about 30,000 to 15,000 years old.
facts.zh: 台東長濱八仙洞出土的石器屬於長濱文化；國立臺灣史前文化博物館稱它是「臺灣最古老的史前文化」。考古發掘顯示，那裡的舊石器時代地層大約是 3 萬到 1.5 萬年前的。
facts.src: 國立自然科學博物館〈再訪八仙洞考古遺址〉(2023)

facts.k_en: A land bridge to the mainland
facts.en: The National Museum of Prehistory explains that in the ice age the lower sea level in the Taiwan Strait formed a land bridge to the Asian mainland, and that about 12,000 years ago, as the ice retreated, the strait formed again and separated the two.
facts.zh: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館說明：冰河時期臺灣海峽的海水面降低，形成與亞洲大陸相連的陸橋；大約 1.2 萬年前冰河消退，臺灣海峽形成，隔開了兩地。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館・臺灣史前文化雲

facts.en: Fishing boats dragging nets along the seafloor near Penghu have brought up many fossils, the remains of animals that lived there when it was land. One is a human jaw called Penghu 1. In 2025, a study of its proteins identified it as a Denisovan man. Its age is uncertain because it was not found in the ground: either 10,000 to 70,000 or 130,000 to 190,000 years.
facts.zh: 在澎湖附近海底拖網作業的漁船，撈起過許多化石，是那裡還是陸地的時候生活在當地的動物留下的。其中有一塊人的下顎，叫做「澎湖一號」。2025 年，一項分析蛋白質的研究確認它屬於一位丹尼索瓦人男性。因為它不是從地層裡挖出來的，年代不確定：可能是 1 萬到 7 萬年前，也可能是 13 萬到 19 萬年前。
facts.src: Tsutaya et al., Science (2025)

facts.en: For decades, schoolbooks said the oldest human fossils in Taiwan were those of “Zuozhen Man” from Tainan, thought to be 20,000 to 30,000 years old. In 2015, researchers at the National Taiwan Museum reported that new radiocarbon tests put the skull pieces at only about 3,000 years old.
facts.zh: 幾十年來，課本都說台灣最古老的人類化石是台南的「左鎮人」，年代被認為有 2 萬到 3 萬年。2015 年，國立臺灣博物館的研究人員表示，重新做的放射性碳定年顯示那些頭骨碎片只有大約 3,000 年。

links.en: Taiwan's Story, Lesson 1: How Do We Know What Happened Long Ago?
links.zh: 台灣歷史第一課：很久以前的事，我們怎麼知道？

links.en: Taiwan's Story, Lesson 2: Who Lived in Taiwan Thousands of Years Ago?
links.zh: 台灣歷史第二課：幾千年前，誰住在台灣？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Evidence · 證據背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A mine, a lakeshore, a tiny bone, and a canoe
culture_cards.title_zh: 一座礦坑、一片湖岸、一小塊骨頭，和一艘獨木舟
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how this history was found, and about the people who lived it.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事：這段歷史是怎麼被找到的，以及活在其中的人。

cards.en: A hundred thousand years, added overnight
cards.body_en: In the early 1960s, mining at Jebel Irhoud uncovered human bones, and for decades nobody could be sure how old they were. A new dig found more bones and burned flint tools that could be dated. In 2017 the team announced an age of about 315,000 years. That was about 100,000 years older than the oldest fossils of our species known until then, which came from East Africa; the new record holder lay in the far northwest of the continent.
cards.body_zh: 1960 年代初，傑貝爾依羅的採礦工程挖出了人骨，幾十年來沒有人能確定它們有多古老。新的發掘找到了更多骨頭，還有可以拿來定年的、被火燒過的燧石石器。2017 年，研究團隊宣布年代大約是 31.5 萬年前——比當時已知最古老的智人化石（來自東非）早了大約十萬年，而新的紀錄保持者位在非洲大陸的最西北邊。

cards.body_en: At White Sands, people walked across the soft mud beside a lake, and the mud kept their tracks. Most of the footprints studied so far were made by teenagers and children. Mammoths and giant ground sloths left tracks in the same mud. Fossils are usually bones. These are something rarer: a few minutes of somebody's day.
cards.body_zh: 在白沙，人走過湖邊鬆軟的泥地，泥巴留住了他們的足跡。目前研究過的腳印，大多是青少年和小孩留下的。長毛象和巨型地懶也在同一片泥地上留下了足跡。化石通常是骨頭；這些腳印更少見——它們是某個人一天裡的幾分鐘。

cards.zh: 從古老的骨頭裡讀出 DNA
cards.body_en: The Swedish scientist Svante Pääbo spent decades learning how to recover DNA from bones tens of thousands of years old. His team read the Neanderthal genome, and from a small finger bone found in a Siberian cave they identified a kind of human nobody had known about, the Denisovans. In 2022 he received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
cards.body_zh: 瑞典科學家帕博（Svante Pääbo）花了幾十年，研究怎麼從幾萬年前的骨頭裡取出 DNA。他的團隊讀出了尼安德塔人的基因體，又從西伯利亞一處洞穴裡發現的一小塊指骨，認出了一種以前沒有人知道的人類：丹尼索瓦人。2022 年，他獲得諾貝爾生理醫學獎。

cards.k: About 1250 CE · 大約西元 1250 年
cards.body_en: By about 3,000 years ago, people had sailed to islands deep in the Pacific such as Vanuatu. Much later, between about 1190 and 1290 CE, voyagers in sailing canoes reached the farthest corners of the Pacific within a few generations: Hawaii, Rapa Nui, and New Zealand. The ancestors of the Māori settled New Zealand at about the time castles and cathedrals were being built in Europe.
cards.body_zh: 大約 3,000 年前，人類已經航行到太平洋深處的島嶼，例如萬那杜。很久以後，大約在西元 1190 到 1290 年之間，駕著風帆獨木舟的航海者在幾代人的時間裡，抵達了太平洋最遠的幾個角落：夏威夷、拉帕努伊（復活節島）和紐西蘭。毛利人的祖先在紐西蘭定居的時候，歐洲正在蓋城堡和大教堂。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (October 2018). The curriculum's world history begins with early cultures in Africa and West Asia; it has no entry on how the first humans spread across the world. So this lesson is background for those entries, not a match for any one of them.
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）。課綱的世界史從非洲與西亞的早期文化開始，沒有談「最早的人類怎麼擴散到世界各地」的條目。所以這一課是這些條目的背景知識，並不直接對應其中任何一條。

items.area: 國中・歷史的基礎觀念
items.area_en: Junior high · basic ideas in history
items.note_en: This lesson introduces BCE and CE, explains that there is no year zero, and shows on the timeline how short the age of writing is.
items.note_zh: 這一課介紹西元前與西元的寫法、說明沒有「0 年」，並用時間軸讓學生看到有文字的時代有多短。

items.note_en: The “Taiwan at That Time” card ties the world story to the Changbin Culture and to how archaeological dates are obtained.
items.note_zh: 「那時候的台灣」把世界的故事接到長濱文化，以及考古的年代是怎麼得來的。

items.area: 國中・古代文化的遺產
items.area_en: Junior high · the heritage of ancient cultures
items.text: 非洲與西亞的早期文化。
items.note_en: World history in the curriculum starts here. This lesson explains how people came to be living in those regions, and everywhere else, long before.
items.note_zh: 課綱的世界史從這裡開始。這一課說明在那之前很久，人是怎麼來到這些地區、以及其他每一個地方的。

myths.myth_en: Humans evolved from monkeys.
myths.myth_zh: 人是從猴子變來的。
myths.fact_en: Humans are not descended from monkeys or from any other primate living today. Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor that lived between about 8 and 6 million years ago; since then the two lines have each gone their own way. Chimpanzees are our cousins, not our grandparents.
myths.fact_zh: 人不是猴子的後代，也不是今天任何一種靈長類的後代。人和黑猩猩有一個共同的祖先，生活在大約 800 萬到 600 萬年前；從那以後，兩條支系各走各的路。黑猩猩是我們的表親，不是我們的祖父母。

myths.myth_en: Human evolution was a straight line, with one kind of human turning into the next.
myths.myth_zh: 人類的演化是一直線，一種人變成下一種人。
myths.fact_en: It was more like a bushy tree. Scientists recognize some 15 to 20 species of early humans, often two or more lived at the same time, and most of them left no living descendants.
myths.fact_zh: 它比較像一棵枝葉茂密的樹。科學家認出大約 15 到 20 種早期的人類，常常有兩種以上同時存在，而且大多數都沒有留下活到今天的後代。

myths.myth_en: Neanderthals were our ancestors, and they were slow and dim.
myths.myth_zh: 尼安德塔人是我們的祖先，而且又笨又遲鈍。
myths.fact_en: Neanderthals were close relatives, not our direct ancestors, although many people today carry a little of their DNA. Their brains were at least as large as ours, in keeping with their sturdy bodies, and the Natural History Museum in London describes them as “very intelligent and accomplished humans.”
myths.fact_zh: 尼安德塔人是我們的近親，不是直系祖先，雖然今天很多人身上帶著一點點他們的 DNA。他們的腦至少和我們一樣大，和他們粗壯的身體相稱；倫敦自然史博物館形容他們是「非常聰明、很有本事的人類」。

myths.myth_en: In the ice age, people could walk anywhere, because land bridges joined all the continents.
myths.myth_zh: 冰河時期到處都有陸橋，人可以走到任何地方。
myths.fact_en: Land bridges appeared only where the sea was shallow. To reach Australia, people had to make several sea crossings, at least one of them close to 100 kilometers. The islands of the remote Pacific were never joined to anything.
myths.fact_zh: 只有海很淺的地方才會出現陸橋。要到澳洲，人們得渡好幾次海，其中至少有一段將近 100 公里。太平洋深處的島嶼，從來沒有和任何陸地相連過。

tricks.body_en: For most of our species' 300,000 years, nearly everyone lived in Africa. The spread across the rest of the world came in the last quarter of that time.
tricks.body_zh: 我們這個物種的 30 萬年裡，大部分時間幾乎所有人都住在非洲。走到世界其他地方，是最後四分之一的時間才發生的事。

tricks.title_en: Ice up, sea down, bridges out
tricks.body_en: When ice sheets grow, the sea falls and shallow seafloor becomes land. When the ice melts, the bridges drown again.
tricks.body_zh: 冰層變大，海面就下降，淺淺的海底變成陸地。冰一融化，陸橋又被淹沒。

tricks.body_en: Fossils show the body. Tools show that people were there. DNA shows who is related to whom. Use all three, and remember what none of them can tell.
tricks.body_zh: 化石看身體，石器看「有人來過」，DNA 看誰和誰有親緣關係。三種一起用，也要記得有些事三種都說不出來。

tricks.body_en: Dates this old come as ranges. A range is not a failure to know; it is an exact statement of how much is known.
tricks.body_zh: 這麼古老的年代，都是一段範圍。範圍不代表「不知道」，而是精確地說出「知道多少」。

activities.title_zh: 一條 30 公尺的時間軸

materials.en: A rope or a strip of paper tape 30 meters long (a hallway or playground works well)
materials.zh: 一條 30 公尺長的繩子或紙膠帶（走廊或操場都很適合）

materials.en: A tape measure, clothespins or sticky notes, and markers
materials.zh: 捲尺、曬衣夾或便利貼、彩色筆

steps.en: Lay out the rope. One end is 300,000 years ago; the other end is today. That makes 1 meter equal to 10,000 years, and 1 centimeter equal to 100 years.
steps.zh: 把繩子拉直。一端是 30 萬年前，另一端是今天。這樣 1 公尺就是 1 萬年，1 公分就是 100 年。

steps.en: In English, read out each event from the parallel timeline and work out together where it goes. For a range, clip two pins and say “between … and …”.
steps.zh: 用英文唸出平行時間軸上的每一件事，一起算出它該放在哪裡。遇到範圍就夾兩個夾子，並且說「between … and …」。

steps.en: Mark the first writing, about 5,300 years ago. It is only 53 centimeters from the end.
steps.zh: 標出最早的文字（大約 5,300 年前）。它離終點只有 53 公分。

steps.en: Ask each student to stand where one event is and say one sentence about it, using a phrase from the History English card.
steps.zh: 請每位學生站到一件事的位置上，用「歷史英語」卡裡的一個句型說一句話。

activities.tip_en: Ask before you measure: “Where do you think writing begins?” Most people guess much too far from the end. The surprise is the lesson.
activities.tip_zh: 量之前先問：「你覺得文字是從哪裡開始的？」大多數人都會猜得離終點太遠。那一下驚訝，就是這堂課要教的東西。

materials.en: For each group, an envelope with three “finds”: a picture of a bone, a pebble or a picture of a stone tool, and a card that says “DNA: shares some DNA with people living far to the east”
materials.zh: 每組一個信封，裡面有三樣「出土物」：一張骨頭的圖片、一顆小石頭或石器的圖片、一張寫著「DNA：和住在很遠的東邊的人有一部分相同」的卡片

materials.en: A sheet with two columns: “We can say” and “We cannot say”
materials.zh: 一張分成兩欄的紙：「我們可以說」和「我們不能說」

steps.en: Tell the class that these three things were found in one cave. Each group studies its envelope for five minutes.
steps.zh: 告訴全班：這三樣東西是在同一個洞穴裡發現的。每一組花五分鐘研究信封裡的東西。

steps.en: Groups write at least three sentences in each column, in English. For example: “We can say that people were here.” “We cannot say what language they spoke.”
steps.zh: 各組用英文在兩欄各寫至少三句。例如：「We can say that people were here.」「We cannot say what language they spoke.」

steps.en: Now give every group one new clue: “A second team dated the cave and got a different age.” Ask what they would want to check before choosing.
steps.zh: 接著發給每組一條新線索：「另一個團隊替這個洞穴定年，得到不一樣的年代。」問他們在做選擇之前，會想先查清楚什麼。

steps.en: Share the lists. Keep the “cannot say” column on the wall for the rest of the series.
steps.zh: 各組分享清單。把「我們不能說」那一欄貼在牆上，整個系列都留著。

activities.tip_en: There is no single right answer to step 3. The aim is for students to ask good questions: How was it dated? What exactly was dated? Could things have moved between layers?
activities.tip_zh: 第三步沒有標準答案。目標是讓學生問出好問題：是怎麼定年的？定的到底是什麼東西？東西有沒有可能在地層之間移動過？

links.en: Why Did People Start Farming?
links.zh: 人為什麼開始種田？
links.note_en: For most of this lesson's 300,000 years, everyone lived by gathering plants and hunting. Lesson 2 asks why people in several parts of the world began to grow their food, and what they gained and lost.
links.note_zh: 這一課講的 30 萬年裡，大部分時間所有人都靠採集和打獵生活。第二課要問：為什麼世界上好幾個地方的人開始自己種食物？他們得到了什麼、又失去了什麼？

links.k_zh: 地球與天氣・第十四課
links.en: How Do Fossils Form?
links.zh: 化石是怎麼形成的？
links.note_en: Why so few living things ever become fossils, and what has to happen for a bone to last.
links.note_zh: 為什麼只有極少數的生物會變成化石，以及一塊骨頭要經過什麼才能保存下來。

links.k_zh: 地球與天氣・第十五課
links.en: How Do We Know How Old the Earth Is?
links.zh: 我們怎麼知道地球幾歲？
links.note_en: How layers and radioactive “clocks” give ages, including the radiocarbon method used at many sites in this lesson.
links.note_zh: 地層和放射性的「時鐘」怎麼告訴我們年代，包括這一課許多遺址用到的放射性碳定年。

links.en: Why Is Every Flat Map Wrong?
links.zh: 為什麼每一張平面地圖都是「錯」的？
links.note_en: Why this series uses a globe: on a flat map, the routes across the far north and the Pacific would be badly stretched.
links.note_zh: 為什麼這個系列用地球儀：在平面地圖上，穿過極北和太平洋的路線會被拉得很變形。

lessons.sources_note_en: Checked October 2026. Dates for this period change as new finds are published; each figure in the lesson comes from the source listed here
lessons.sources_note_zh: 2026 年 10 月查證。這個時期的年代會隨著新的發現而改變；課文裡的每一個數字都出自下面列的資料

sources.zh: 智人大約 30 萬年前在非洲出現

sources.zh: 走出非洲、較早的幾群人、歐洲、澳洲、亞洲、美洲「仍在爭論」、尼安德塔人與丹尼索瓦人的 DNA

sources.zh: 奧莫基比什：至少 23.3 萬年前；較早的數字約 19.5 到 19.7 萬年

sources.zh: 阿皮迪瑪洞穴：超過 21 萬年

sources.zh: 馬杰貝貝「至少 6.5 萬年」的說法

sources.zh: 蒙哥湖：兩處墓葬都在大約 4 萬年前（誤差 2 千年）；澳洲最古老的人類遺骸

sources.en: The case that people reached Australia no more than about 50,000 years ago
sources.zh: 主張人類抵達澳洲不早於大約 5 萬年前的看法
sources.src: University of Utah, “When did humans first colonize Australia?” (2025)

sources.en: Sea crossings to Sahul, at least one approaching 100 km
sources.zh: 到莎湖陸棚要渡海，至少有一段將近 100 公里

sources.en: Bacho Kiro Cave: our species in Europe before 45,000 years ago
sources.zh: 巴喬基羅洞穴：4.5 萬年前智人已在歐洲

sources.en: Grotte Mandrin: 56,800 to 51,700 years ago
sources.zh: 曼德林岩棚：5.68 萬到 5.17 萬年前

sources.en: Tam Pa Ling, Laos: our species present by 70 ± 3 thousand years
sources.zh: 寮國譚巴玲洞穴：7 萬年前（誤差 3 千年）已有智人

sources.en: Tianyuan Cave: a 40,000-year-old person and their DNA
sources.zh: 田園洞：4 萬年前的人與其 DNA
sources.src: Fu et al., PNAS 110 (2013); Shang et al., PNAS 104 (2007)

sources.en: White Sands footprints: about 23,000 to 21,000 years ago
sources.zh: 白沙腳印：大約 2.3 萬到 2.1 萬年前
sources.src: Bennett et al., Science 373 (2021); U.S. National Park Service

sources.en: The second dating of the White Sands footprints, and the criticism of the first
sources.zh: 白沙腳印的第二次定年，以及對第一次定年的批評
sources.src: Pigati et al., Science 382 (2023); Madsen et al., Science 375 (2022)

sources.en: Monte Verde: the excavators' date of about 14,500 years
sources.zh: 蒙特維德：發掘團隊定的年代，大約 1.45 萬年前
sources.src: Dillehay et al., Science 320 (2008); Dillehay et al., PLOS ONE 10 (2015)

sources.en: Monte Verde: the 2026 study arguing for an age of about 8,000 to 4,000 years
sources.zh: 蒙特維德：2026 年主張年代只有大約 8,000 到 4,000 年的研究

sources.en: The ice-free corridor opened about 13,800 years ago
sources.zh: 無冰通道大約 1.38 萬年前打開

sources.en: East Polynesia: Society Islands about 1025 to 1120 CE; the remaining islands, including New Zealand, about 1190 to 1290 CE
sources.zh: 東玻里尼西亞：社會群島約西元 1025–1120 年；其餘島嶼（含紐西蘭）約西元 1190–1290 年

sources.en: Ice sheets at their maximum from 26,500 to about 19,000 or 20,000 years ago
sources.zh: 冰層最大的時期：2.65 萬到大約 1.9 或 2 萬年前

sources.en: Sea level about 125 m lower about 21,000 years ago; another study gives 134 m
sources.zh: 大約 2.1 萬年前海面比現在低約 125 公尺；另一項研究是 134 公尺
sources.src: U.S. Geological Survey, Fact Sheet 2005-3056; Lambeck et al., PNAS 111 (2014)

sources.en: Beringia: a wide plain, at its widest about 21,000 years ago
sources.zh: 白令陸橋：一片寬廣的平原，大約 2.1 萬年前最寬

sources.en: Dating methods: radiocarbon (to about 50,000 years), luminescence, uranium-series
sources.zh: 定年方法：放射性碳（大約 5 萬年以內）、螢光、鈾系

sources.en: Neanderthals: 1 to 4 percent of the DNA of people of Eurasian descent; Denisovans
sources.zh: 尼安德塔人：占歐亞血統的人 DNA 的 1% 到 4%；丹尼索瓦人
sources.src: Smithsonian Human Origins Program, “Ancient DNA and Neanderthals”

sources.en: Svante Pääbo, Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2022
sources.zh: 帕博，2022 年諾貝爾生理醫學獎

lessons.title: Why Did People Start Farming?
lessons.blurb_en: Follow one river valley through a year: foragers who move with the seasons on one bank, an early farming village on the other. Then see on a map how farming began separately in many parts of the world, and weigh what people gained and what they gave up.
lessons.blurb_zh: 跟著一座河谷過一年：一岸是跟著季節搬家的採集狩獵者，另一岸是早期的農村。再從地圖上看農業怎麼在世界上好幾個地方各自開始，並且想一想人們得到了什麼、又放棄了什麼。
lessons.big_idea_en: Farming was not invented once, by one person, or in one place. Beginning about 12,000 years ago, people in many parts of the world slowly turned wild plants and animals into crops and herds. It brought more food and more people, and it brought new hardships too.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 農業不是一次發明的，不是一個人發明的，也不是在一個地方發明的。從大約 1.2 萬年前開始，世界上好幾個地方的人各自慢慢把野生的植物和動物變成作物和牲畜。它帶來更多的食物、更多的人，也帶來了新的辛苦。

lab.title_en: One River, Two Ways to Live
lab.title_zh: 同一條河，兩種過日子的方法
lab.how_en: On the left bank lives a band of foragers, people who gather wild plants, fish, and hunt. On the right bank is an early farming village. Press Play, or pull the slider, and watch both through one year. Notice who moves and who stays, when each group works hardest, and what happens to the grain in the granary. Then switch on “A year when the harvest fails.” This valley is an illustration, not a real place: it is here to show the difference between two ways of getting food.
lab.how_zh: 河的左岸住著一群採集狩獵的人，靠採野生植物、捕魚和打獵過活。右岸是一座早期的農村。按「播放」或拉動滑桿，看兩邊怎麼過同一年。注意誰在搬家、誰留在原地，兩邊各在什麼時候最忙，還有穀倉裡的穀子怎麼變化。然後打開「歉收的一年」。這座河谷是示意，不是真實的地方：它只是用來讓你看到兩種取得食物的方法有什麼不同。
lab.bar_note_en: The two bars only show more or less. They are not measurements.
lab.bar_note_zh: 這兩條長條只表示「多一點、少一點」，不是量出來的數字。
lab.bad_note_en: In this year the rain does not come and the crop withers. The village has put nearly all its work into two fields, so the granary runs out before the next harvest. The foragers are short of food too, but they eat many different things and can move to where food is. This is one common pattern, not a rule: foragers also went hungry, and farmers found ways to protect themselves, such as storing extra grain, planting several crops, and sharing with relatives.
lab.bad_note_zh: 這一年雨沒有來，作物枯了。村子把幾乎所有的力氣都放在兩塊田上，所以穀倉在下一次收成之前就空了。採集狩獵的人食物也變少，但他們吃的東西種類多，也可以搬到有食物的地方。這是常見的一種情形，不是定律：採集狩獵的人也會挨餓，農人也想出了保護自己的辦法，例如多存一些穀子、多種幾種作物、和親戚互相分享。

seasons.forager_en: Camped beside the river. They fish, dig roots, and pick young leaves and shoots. The whole camp can be carried, so it goes where the food is.
seasons.forager_zh: 在河邊紮營。捕魚、挖根莖、採嫩葉和嫩芽。整個營地都搬得動，食物在哪裡，就搬到哪裡。
seasons.farmer_en: Breaking the soil and sowing seed saved from last year. If the seed grain is eaten, there is nothing to plant, so some food must always be kept back.
seasons.farmer_zh: 翻土，把去年留下來的種子播下去。種子要是吃掉了就沒得種，所以一定得留下一部分糧食不吃。
seasons.forager_bad_en: Camped beside the river as usual. Fish and roots do not depend on this year's rain as much as a field does.
seasons.forager_bad_zh: 照常在河邊紮營。魚和根莖不像田那樣依賴今年的雨水。
seasons.farmer_bad_en: The granary is empty before the new crop is ready. This gap is the hungry season. People borrow from relatives, gather wild plants, and hunt, as their ancestors did.
seasons.farmer_bad_zh: 新的作物還沒熟，穀倉已經空了。這段青黃不接的日子最難熬。大家向親戚借糧、採野菜、打獵，就像他們的祖先一樣。

seasons.forager_en: Moved to the open meadow. They gather wild seeds and berries and hunt. Many foods come ready at different times, so no single one has to feed everyone.
seasons.forager_zh: 搬到開闊的草地。採野生的種子和莓果，也打獵。很多種食物在不同的時候成熟，所以不必靠單一種食物養活所有人。
seasons.farmer_en: The crop is growing, and so are the weeds. People weed, scare off birds, carry water, and watch the goats. The field cannot be left alone.
seasons.farmer_zh: 作物在長，雜草也在長。大家除草、趕鳥、提水、看顧山羊。田不能丟著不管。
seasons.forager_bad_en: The meadow is dry and the berries are few. The band moves on sooner and spreads out more widely to look for food.
seasons.forager_bad_zh: 草地乾了，莓果很少。這一群人提早搬走，分散到更大的範圍去找食物。
seasons.farmer_bad_en: No rain. The crop stays short and turns brown. The village cannot simply walk away: its houses, its stored things, and its fields are all here.
seasons.farmer_bad_zh: 沒有下雨。作物長不高，慢慢枯黃。村子沒辦法說走就走：房子、存放的東西和田都在這裡。

seasons.forager_en: In the woods for the nut harvest. Nuts keep well, so some are stored for winter, but only as much as people can carry or come back for.
seasons.forager_zh: 到樹林裡撿堅果。堅果耐放，所以會存一些過冬，但只存搬得動、或之後回得來拿的份量。
seasons.farmer_en: Harvest, the busiest weeks of the year. Everyone cuts, carries, threshes, and fills the granary. One good harvest can feed the village until the next.
seasons.farmer_zh: 收割，一年裡最忙的幾個星期。所有人都在割、搬、打穀、把穀倉裝滿。一次好收成，可以讓全村吃到下一次收成。
seasons.forager_bad_en: The nut harvest is thinner than usual. They store a little less and plan to rely more on hunting.
seasons.forager_bad_zh: 堅果比往年少。存下來的少一點，打算多靠打獵。
seasons.farmer_bad_en: A poor harvest. The granary is not even half full, and part of it has to be saved as seed for next spring.
seasons.farmer_bad_zh: 收成很差。穀倉連一半都沒裝滿，其中一部分還得留下來當明年春天的種子。

seasons.forager_en: A sheltered winter camp. They eat stored nuts, set traps, hunt, and mend tools. Food is harder to find, and winter is the lean time.
seasons.forager_zh: 在背風的地方過冬。吃存下來的堅果、設陷阱、打獵、修理工具。食物比較難找，冬天是吃緊的季節。
seasons.farmer_en: Living on stored grain. People grind it every day, repair houses, and care for the animals. The granary slowly empties, and everyone can see how much is left.
seasons.farmer_zh: 靠存糧過日子。每天磨穀子、修房子、照顧牲口。穀倉一天一天變空，剩下多少大家都看得到。
seasons.forager_bad_en: A hard winter. With fewer stored nuts, they hunt and trap more, and may join relatives in another valley.
seasons.forager_bad_zh: 難過的冬天。存的堅果少了，就多打獵、多設陷阱，也可能去投靠另一個河谷的親戚。
seasons.farmer_bad_en: The grain is being eaten carefully. Meals are smaller, and the village counts how many weeks are left.
seasons.farmer_bad_zh: 穀子吃得很省。每一餐都變少，全村都在算還撐得了幾個星期。

legend.en: Foragers (their camp moves with the seasons)
legend.zh: 採集狩獵的人（營地跟著季節搬）

legend.en: Farmers (their village stays in one place)
legend.zh: 農人（村子固定在一個地方）

legend.en: The crop: green while growing, golden when ripe
legend.zh: 作物：生長時是綠的，成熟時變金黃

legend.en: Stored grain in the granary
legend.zh: 穀倉裡的存糧

lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch, not a reconstruction of any real site. The landscape, houses, crop, and the four seasons (sow in spring, harvest in autumn) are simplified; in many of the places where farming began, the farming year ran differently. Real foragers and real farmers were also far more varied than these two groups: some foragers lived in one place all year, and many early farmers went on gathering and hunting.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意，不是任何真實遺址的復原。地景、房屋、作物和四季（春天播種、秋天收割）都經過簡化；在許多最早開始種田的地方，農事的時間並不是這樣安排的。真實的採集狩獵者和農人也比這兩群人多樣得多：有些採集狩獵者整年住在同一個地方，而許多早期的農人仍然繼續採集和打獵。
lab.credit_html: Model: an illustration made for this lesson. It does not show a real place or a real people. 模型：為這一課製作的示意，畫的不是真實的地點或族群。

paras: Think about what you ate today. Rice, bread, noodles, vegetables, eggs: nearly all of it came from a farm. Yet for most of the 300,000 years of our species, there were no farms anywhere. People gathered wild plants, fished, and hunted. Then, starting about 12,000 years ago, people in some places began to plant seeds and to keep animals. It was one of the biggest changes in human history. Why did it happen?

The first surprise is that it happened more than once. Farming began independently in at least eleven regions of the world, among people who did not learn it from one another. In West Asia they grew wheat and barley. In China it was millet in the north and rice in the south. In the Americas it was squash and maize. In New Guinea it was bananas and taro, and in Africa sorghum. Each group worked with the wild plants that grew nearby.

The second surprise is how slow it was. Nobody woke up one morning as a farmer. Wild wheat drops its seeds when they are ripe, which is good for the plant and bad for the person trying to collect them. A few plants hold on to their seeds. Most researchers think the change went like this: when people cut the grain and sowed some of it again, those were the seeds they carried home, so each year a few more plants were of that kind. For wheat, barley, and rice, it took about two to four thousand years before nearly all the plants kept their seeds. All that time, people went on gathering and hunting as well.

Why did people begin? Researchers do not agree. Some point to the climate: the last ice age ended about 11,700 years ago, and the weather became warmer and steadier; only then, they argue, did farming become possible. Others think that growing numbers of people needed more food. Others note that some foragers were already living in villages before they farmed, or that people were gathering in large numbers for feasts. The reasons may well have been different in different places.

Farming changed people's lives, and not only for the better. A field can feed more people than the same land left wild, and the number of people grew. But in most places that have been studied, skeletons show that people became shorter as farming took hold, a sign of poorer food or more sickness. Stored grain could be owned, and the gap between richer and poorer families widened. A farmer is also tied to the field. When a harvest failed, it was much harder to move away.

Farming spread in two ways. Sometimes farmers moved into new lands and took their seeds and animals with them. Sometimes foragers learned from their neighbors. And some peoples kept other ways of getting food for thousands of years. About 5,000 years ago, people in Taiwan were growing both millet and rice. Today almost everything we eat is farmed, and few of us ever wonder who first tamed the plants on our plates.
paras_zh: 想想你今天吃了什麼。飯、麵包、麵條、青菜、蛋：幾乎全都來自農場。可是在我們這個物種三十萬年的歷史裡，大部分時間世界上根本沒有農場。人們採野生的植物、捕魚、打獵。後來，從大約 1.2 萬年前開始，有些地方的人開始播種、養動物。這是人類歷史上最大的改變之一。為什麼會這樣？
第一件讓人意外的事：它不只發生一次。農業至少在世界上十一個地區各自獨立地開始，這些地方的人並不是互相學來的。西亞種的是小麥和大麥。中國北方是小米和黍，南方是稻。美洲是南瓜和玉米。新幾內亞是香蕉和芋頭，非洲是高粱。每一群人用的都是身邊長的野生植物。

第二件讓人意外的事：它非常慢。沒有人是某一天早上醒來就變成農夫的。野生的小麥種子熟了會自己掉到地上——這對植物是好事，對想把種子收集起來的人卻是麻煩。有少數幾株的種子會留在穗上。多數研究者認為變化是這樣發生的：人們割下穀子、再把其中一些播回地裡的時候，帶回家的正是這種種子，所以每一年，這種植株就多一點點。以小麥、大麥和稻來說，要等到幾乎所有植株的種子都留在穗上，花了大約兩千到四千年。在這麼長的時間裡，人們也一直繼續採集和打獵。
人為什麼開始種田？研究者的看法並不一致。有人認為是氣候：上一次冰河時期大約在 1.17 萬年前結束，天氣變得比較暖、比較穩定——他們主張，要到這時候種田才成為可能。有人認為是人越來越多，需要更多食物。也有人指出，有些採集狩獵的人還沒開始種田就已經住在村子裡了，或是人們會大批聚在一起舉行宴會。在不同的地方，原因很可能並不一樣。
農業改變了人的生活，而且不是只往好的方向。一塊田能養活的人，比同一塊地放著不管時多，人口也跟著增加。但是在大多數研究過的地方，骨骸顯示人在農業站穩之後變矮了——這表示吃得比較差，或是比較常生病。存起來的穀子可以被「擁有」，比較富有和比較貧窮的家庭之間的差距變大了。農人也被綁在田上：收成不好的時候，要搬走困難得多。
農業用兩種方式傳開。有時候是農人搬到新的地方，把種子和牲畜一起帶過去。有時候是採集狩獵的人向鄰居學的。也有一些人群，幾千年來一直用別的方法取得食物。大約五千年前，台灣已經有人同時種小米和稻。今天我們吃的東西幾乎全是種出來、養出來的，卻很少有人想過，盤子裡的植物最早是誰馴化的。
questions: The lesson says farming was not invented once. What is the evidence for that?
Why did it take thousands of years to turn wild wheat into a crop?
The lesson calls farming a trade. What did people gain, and what did they give up?
answers: Farming began in many regions that had no contact with one another, each with its own plants: wheat and barley in West Asia, millet and rice in China, squash and maize in the Americas, bananas and taro in New Guinea, sorghum in Africa. A review counts at least eleven such regions.

Because the change came from small differences added up over many harvests. Only a few wild plants keep their seeds on the stalk. Each time people cut and resowed the grain, slightly more of the seed came from those plants. People were also still gathering and hunting, so the fields were only part of how they lived.

They gained more food from the same land, stored food for hard seasons, and larger families and villages. They gave up some of their freedom to move, took on more risk when a harvest failed, and in many places their health became poorer. Differences in wealth between families also grew.

Once, in West Asia, and it spread from there
Once, in China, and it spread from there
Twice: once in Asia and once in Europe

quiz.q: Why is wild wheat hard to collect?
options: Its ripe seeds fall to the ground by themselves
It grows only on high mountains
Its seeds are poisonous until cooked
It ripens only once every ten years

What does the evidence show about the bodies of early farmers in most places studied?

They were much taller than the foragers before them
Their bones have never been found
