lessons.title: Why Did the First Cities Grow Beside Rivers?
lessons.title_zh: 最早的城市為什麼都在河邊？
lessons.blurb_en: Raise the Great Pyramid course by course in 3D and test four ideas about how its blocks were lifted. Then find on a map the rivers where the first cities grew, and sort out what a river gave a city, and what trouble it brought.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 裡一層一層蓋起大金字塔，試試四種「石頭怎麼運上去」的想法。再從地圖上找出最早的城市長在哪些河邊，分一分河帶給城市什麼、又帶來什麼麻煩。
lessons.big_idea_en: The first cities grew where rivers made it possible to farm enough food for many people who did not farm. But every river behaved differently, and every city had to learn to live with its own river. Rivers made cities possible, not certain.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 最早的城市長在河流讓人能種出足夠糧食的地方，多到可以養活許多不種田的人。但每一條河的脾氣都不一樣，每一座城市都得學會跟自己的河相處。河讓城市成為可能，卻不保證一定會有城市。

lab.title_en: How Was the Great Pyramid Built? Four Ideas
lab.title_zh: 大金字塔是怎麼蓋起來的？四種想法
lab.how_en: Pull the slider and the pyramid rises course by course. Watch the number marked in gold: when the pyramid is only half as tall as it will be, almost nine-tenths of its stone is already in place. Then switch between four ideas about how the blocks were raised. Each is a hypothesis that researchers have proposed, with evidence for it and problems against it; no one knows for certain which, or which mix, was used.
lab.how_zh: 拉動滑桿，金字塔會一層一層長高。注意金色的那個數字：金字塔蓋到最後高度的一半時，將近九成的石頭已經放上去了。接著切換四種「石塊怎麼運上去」的想法。每一種都是研究者提出的假說，有支持的證據，也有說不通的地方；到底用的是哪一種、或是好幾種混用，沒有人能確定。
lab.numbers_note_en: The pyramid's size follows published measurements. The ramp's slope (1 in 10, which one study calls the most practical) and its width of 20 meters are assumptions made for this sketch, so the ramp numbers show the size of the problem, not a measured fact.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 金字塔的大小依照已發表的測量。坡道的坡度（每升高 1 公尺走 10 公尺，有一份研究認為這是最實際的坡度）和 20 公尺的寬度是這個示意圖的假設，所以坡道的數字只是讓你看到問題有多大，不是量出來的事實。

ideas.what_en: A single ramp runs straight up to one face, and it is raised and lengthened as the pyramid grows.
ideas.what_zh: 一條坡道直直通到金字塔的一面，金字塔長高，它就跟著加高、加長。
ideas.for_en: It is the simplest idea, and small ramps of this kind were probably used for the lowest courses.
ideas.for_zh: 這是最簡單的想法；最下面幾層，很可能真的用過這種小坡道。
ideas.against_en: At a slope of 1 in 10 it would have been about 1.5 kilometers long. One estimate says it would have needed more than three times the material of the pyramid itself, and no such mound has been found.
ideas.against_zh: 以每升高 1 公尺走 10 公尺的坡度計算，它會長達大約 1.5 公里。有一個估計認為，它需要的材料是金字塔本身的三倍以上，而且沒有找到這樣的土堆。
ideas.src: Edwards, Technology and Culture 44 (2003); Brier, Archaeology (2007)

ideas.en: A zigzag ramp on one face
ideas.zh: 在一面上來回折返的坡道
ideas.what_en: The ramp climbs one face of the pyramid, turning back and forth like a mountain path.
ideas.what_zh: 坡道沿著金字塔的一面往上爬，像山路一樣來回轉彎。
ideas.for_en: It needs far less material than a long straight ramp and fits on a crowded building site.
ideas.for_zh: 它需要的材料比長長的直坡道少得多，也擠得進施工的工地。
ideas.against_en: Turning a sledge with a heavy block at every switchback is slow and dangerous, and the ramp covers the face that builders needed to measure.
ideas.against_zh: 每一次折返都要把載著大石頭的雪橇轉過來，又慢又危險；坡道還會蓋住工人需要測量的那一面。
ideas.src: Zigzag ramps are described in Arnold, Building in Egypt (1991), and Lehner, The Complete Pyramids (1997), as cited by Edwards (2003); the drawbacks follow Rosell Roig, arXiv 2511.06112 (2025), a preprint that argues for the author's own model

ideas.en: A ramp that spirals around the outside
ideas.zh: 繞著外面盤旋上去的坡道
ideas.what_en: The ramp wraps around all four faces, the way a mountain road spirals upward.
ideas.what_zh: 坡道繞著四個面盤旋往上，就像繞山的公路。
ideas.for_en: It does away with the need for a ramp more than a kilometer long, which helps explain why no huge ramp has been found.
ideas.for_zh: 它不需要一條一公里多的長坡道，這可以解釋為什麼找不到巨大的坡道。
ideas.against_en: It would hide the corners and edges that builders needed to measure, and teams would have to haul blocks around tight corners.
ideas.against_zh: 它會遮住工人需要測量的角和邊，拖石頭的隊伍也得在很窄的轉角轉彎。
ideas.src: Brier, Archaeology (2007), quoting Dieter Arnold, Building in Egypt; Edwards (2003)

ideas.en: A ramp hidden inside the pyramid
ideas.zh: 藏在金字塔裡面的坡道
ideas.what_en: An outside ramp builds the lowest part, and then a tunnel-like ramp inside the pyramid, just behind the outer face, carries blocks the rest of the way up.
ideas.what_zh: 外面的坡道先蓋最下面的部分，接著由一條藏在金字塔裡面、緊貼外牆的通道式坡道，把石頭一路運上去。
ideas.for_en: The architect Jean-Pierre Houdin points to a density survey from the 1980s that may show such a ramp, and to a notch high on one corner.
ideas.for_zh: 建築師烏丹（Jean-Pierre Houdin）指出，1980 年代的一次密度測量可能顯示出這樣的坡道，在一個角的高處也有一個缺口。
ideas.against_en: It has not been proven. No one has entered such a ramp, and many Egyptologists remain unconvinced.
ideas.against_zh: 這還沒有被證實。沒有人走進過這樣的坡道，許多埃及學家也還沒有被說服。

legend.en: Limestone blocks, drawn as a few thick courses
legend.zh: 石灰岩石塊，畫成幾層厚厚的石層

legend.en: A construction ramp (one hypothesis at a time)
legend.zh: 施工用的坡道（一次顯示一種假說）

legend.en: A sledge hauling a block up the ramp
legend.zh: 拖著石塊上坡的雪橇

lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch. The real pyramid has far more courses than the model shows, and the ramps are drawn from descriptions of each hypothesis, not from plans. The distance to the Nile is shortened.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意。真正的金字塔層數比模型多得多；坡道是依照每一種假說的描述畫的，不是根據任何設計圖。到尼羅河的距離也縮短了。
lab.credit_html: Model: an illustration made for this lesson. Pyramid measurements and the four hypotheses follow the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 模型：為這一課製作的示意。金字塔的尺寸與四種假說，依本頁最下面列出的資料。

paras: In Lesson 2, villages stored grain. In Lesson 3, people in Uruk wrote down who owed what. Uruk was more than a village. It was a city, with temples, workshops, and at least 25,000 people, many of whom did not farm at all. A city needs a lot of extra food, more than its farmers eat. Where could that much food come from?

In most of the places where the first cities grew, the answer was a river. Southern Mesopotamia gets almost no rain, but the Euphrates and Tigris bring water from the mountains. Egypt is mostly desert, but every summer the Nile rose and left fresh mud on its fields. Rivers gave water for crops, soil that stayed rich, fish and reeds, and a road for boats. Heavy loads, from grain to stone, traveled far more easily by water than over land.

Yet the rivers were not alike. The Nile's flood came at about the same time every year, and Egyptian farmers could plan around it. In Mesopotamia the high water came at the wrong time for the crops, so people had to lead water to the fields with canals and dikes. The rivers of the Indus Valley, fed by the summer monsoon, changed over the centuries as their floods and the monsoon rains grew weaker. Along the Yellow River in China, great floods could break through and change the river's course. Each river shaped its city in its own way.

Many textbooks speak of four great river civilizations: Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Indus, and China's Yellow River. The list is a useful start, but it leaves a lot out. Liangzhu, beside the Yangtze, built dams and a walled city more than 5,000 years ago. Caral, in Peru, grew in a desert valley beside the small Supe River at about the same time as the first Egyptian pyramids. Cities began in more places than four, and none of them is the “first” in every way.

Cities could organize huge projects. In Egypt, the Great Pyramid of Khufu rose more than 4,500 years ago, originally about 146 meters tall. It was not built by slaves. Archaeologists have found the town that housed the builders of the Giza pyramids, with bakeries and storerooms. A Harvard project describes the workers as Egyptians paid in food, mainly bread and beer; some researchers think many came in rotating teams from their home districts. Boats carried its fine limestone down the Nile. How the blocks were raised to the top is still not fully known.

Living beside a river had risks. Floods could destroy fields, and a river that changed its path could leave a city without water. The Indus cities declined slowly after about 1900 BCE, and changing river flows are one of the main explanations. A river did not make a city by itself. People did, by learning how their river behaved and working together to manage it.
paras_zh: 第二課的村子會儲存穀子。第三課的烏魯克人會記下誰欠了什麼。烏魯克不只是個村子，它是一座城市，有神廟、作坊，至少兩萬五千人，其中很多人根本不種田。一座城市需要很多多出來的糧食，比種田的人自己吃的還多。這麼多糧食，要從哪裡來？
在大多數最早長出城市的地方，答案是一條河。美索不達米亞南部幾乎不下雨，但幼發拉底河和底格里斯河從山上帶來了水。埃及大部分是沙漠，但尼羅河每年夏天漲水，在田裡留下新的泥土。河流給了灌溉作物的水、保持肥沃的土、魚和蘆葦，還有一條給船走的路。重的東西，從穀子到石頭，走水路比走陸路容易得多。
可是這些河並不一樣。尼羅河每年漲水的時間差不多，埃及的農夫可以照著它安排。在美索不達米亞，漲水的時間跟作物的季節對不上，人們只好用運河和堤防把水引到田裡。印度河流域的河靠夏季的季風供水，幾百年下來，洪水和季風雨都慢慢變弱了。在中國的黃河，大洪水可能沖破河岸，讓河改道。每一條河都用自己的方式塑造它的城市。
很多課本會說有四大河流文明：美索不達米亞、埃及、印度河，和中國的黃河。這份清單是一個好的起點，但漏掉了很多。長江邊的良渚，在五千多年前就建了水壩和有城牆的城市。祕魯的卡拉爾，長在一個沙漠河谷裡，旁邊是小小的蘇佩河，時間和埃及最早的金字塔差不多。城市開始的地方不只四個，也沒有哪一個在每一方面都是「第一」。
城市能組織巨大的工程。在埃及，胡夫的大金字塔在四千五百多年前蓋起來，原本大約 146 公尺高。它不是奴隸蓋的。考古學家找到了吉薩金字塔建造者住的城鎮，有麵包坊和倉庫。哈佛大學的一個計畫說，這些工人是埃及人，領的是食物，主要是麵包和啤酒；也有研究者認為，很多人是從家鄉輪班被徵調來的。船沿著尼羅河運來細緻的石灰岩。石頭是怎麼運到頂端的，到現在還沒有完全弄清楚。
住在河邊也有風險。洪水會毀掉田地，河一改道，城市就可能沒有水。印度河的城市在大約西元前 1900 年以後慢慢衰落，河水流量的改變是主要的解釋之一。河並不會自己變出一座城市。是人學會了自己的河怎麼流、一起合作管理它，城市才出現。
questions: Why does a city need more food than a village, and how did a river help?
How was the Nile's flood different from the floods in Mesopotamia, and why did that matter to farmers?
The lesson says rivers made cities possible, not certain. What else did people need to do?
answers: Many people in a city did not farm, such as priests, craftspeople, and officials, so farmers had to grow more than they ate. A river gave water in dry lands, rich soil, and an easy way to move food by boat.

The Nile rose at about the same time every year, so farmers could plan around it. In Mesopotamia the high water came at the wrong time for the crops, so people had to build canals and dikes to bring water to the fields when it was needed.
They had to learn how their river behaved, work together to dig canals or build dams, store food, and deal with floods and droughts. Without organization, a river alone did not create a city.

vocab.ex: Uruk was one of the first cities in the world.
vocab.exzh: 烏魯克是世界上最早的城市之一。

vocab.ex: The first farmers settled in the river valley.
vocab.exzh: 最早的農夫在河谷裡定居下來。

vocab.ex: The Nile flooded every summer.
vocab.exzh: 尼羅河每年夏天氾濫。

vocab.ex: Irrigation brought river water to the fields.
vocab.exzh: 灌溉把河水帶到田裡。

vocab.ex: A food surplus fed the people who did not farm.
vocab.exzh: 多出來的糧食養活了不種田的人。

vocab.ex: Farmers dug canals to lead water to their crops.
vocab.exzh: 農夫挖水道，把水引到作物那裡。

vocab.ex: The Great Pyramid was built for King Khufu.
vocab.exzh: 大金字塔是為胡夫王蓋的。

vocab.ex: There were more than four early civilizations.
vocab.exzh: 早期的文明不只四個。

quiz.q: Why did the first cities need a lot of extra food?
options: Many people in a city did not farm
People in cities ate twice as much

quiz.q: What did the Nile do every summer?
options: It rose and left fresh mud on the fields

quiz.q: Why was farming harder to organize in southern Mesopotamia?
options: The high water came at the wrong time for the crops
There were no rivers at all
The soil was made of sand only

quiz.q: Who built the Great Pyramid, according to the evidence of their town?
options: Egyptian workers who were given food

quiz.q: Which of these early centers is NOT one of the usual “four river civilizations”?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.en: Half the height, most of the stone
parts.zh: 一半的高度，大部分的石頭
parts.meta_en: A pyramid is heavy at the bottom
parts.text_en: Stop at half the height and read the gold number: almost 88 percent of the stone is already in place. The hardest part is not the bottom but the top, where every block has to go highest.
parts.text_zh: 停在一半的高度，看金色的數字：將近百分之八十八的石頭已經放上去了。最難的不是下面，而是上面，因為那裡每一塊石頭都得抬到最高。

parts.en: The ramp that grows too long
parts.text_en: Watch the straight ramp near the top. At a gentle slope it stretches far into the desert, and the ramp itself becomes a giant building project.
parts.text_zh: 看看直坡道快到頂端的樣子。坡度一平緩，它就伸到沙漠很遠的地方，坡道本身變成另一件巨大的工程。

parts.meta_en: A ramp that wraps the faces
parts.text_en: The spiral needs no long mound, but look at the corners: the ramp covers them, and the turns grow tight and steep near the top.
parts.text_zh: 螺旋坡道不需要長長的土堆，但看看四個角：坡道把它們蓋住了，越往上，轉彎越窄、越陡。

parts.text_en: When it was finished, a casing of fine white limestone made the faces smooth. Most of the casing is gone today, which is why the pyramid now looks stepped and stands a little shorter.
parts.text_zh: 完工的時候，一層細白的石灰岩外殼讓四個面變得平滑。今天這層外殼大部分已經不見了，所以金字塔現在看起來一階一階的，也矮了一點。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try all four ideas yourself. For each one, ask: where would the ramp's material come from, and what would it hide from the builders?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著自己把四種想法都試一遍。每一種都問問：坡道的材料從哪裡來？它會把什麼遮住，讓工人看不到？

centers.en: Where Did the First Cities Grow?
centers.lead_en: Pull the slider from about 6,200 years ago toward the present. Each place lights up when its first cities or large centers appear, faintly while the dates are uncertain and strongly once the evidence is clear. Click a number to read which river it stood beside.
centers.lead_zh: 把滑桿從大約 6,200 年前往現在拉。每個地方在最早的城市或大型中心出現時亮起來：年代還不確定的時候淡淡的，證據明確了才變實。點一個號碼，看看它在哪一條河旁邊。
centers.count_zh: 目前已經有城市的地方

labels.what_en: The river, and what grew there

centers.idle_en: Click a numbered circle on the map, or a name below it.
centers.idle_zh: 點地圖上有號碼的圓，或是地圖下面的名字。
centers.foot_en: Textbooks often speak of four river civilizations. The map shows six places, because the Yangtze in China and the Supe valley in Peru also had very early large centers. Every one of them stood beside a river, but the rivers behaved very differently.
centers.foot_zh: 課本常說有四個大河文明。這張地圖畫了六個地方，因為中國的長江、祕魯的蘇佩河谷也很早就有大型的中心。它們每一個都在河邊，但這些河的脾氣非常不一樣。

centers.zh: 美索不達米亞的烏魯克
centers.crops_en: The Euphrates and Tigris. Uruk grew on a marshy delta plain near the sea, where one recent study suggests the tides helped water the first fields.
centers.crops_zh: 幼發拉底河和底格里斯河。烏魯克長在靠海、沼澤很多的三角洲平原上；一項新的研究認為，最早的田可能是靠潮水幫忙灌溉的。
centers.when_en: The Uruk period, about 4000 to 3200 BCE. At its peak the city held at least 25,000 people, by one cautious estimate.
centers.when_zh: 烏魯克時期，大約西元前 4000 到 3200 年。依一個保守的估計，城市最大時至少住了兩萬五千人。
centers.note_en: UNESCO calls these marshes “the heartland where the first cities flourished.”
centers.note_zh: 聯合國教科文組織稱這片沼澤是「最早的城市興起的核心地帶」。
centers.src: Giosan and Goodman, PLOS ONE (2025); UNESCO, The Ahwar of Southern Iraq

centers.crops_en: The Nile. It flooded every summer and left fresh mud on the fields, so the farming year could follow the river.
centers.crops_zh: 尼羅河。它每年夏天氾濫，在田裡留下新的泥土，所以種田的一年可以跟著河走。
centers.when_en: Memphis is traditionally said to have been founded about 3000 BCE as the capital of a unified Egypt.
centers.when_zh: 傳統的說法是，孟斐斯大約在西元前 3000 年建立，做為統一後的埃及的首都。
centers.note_en: Early Egyptian towns are hard to study: in the Nile Delta, evidence for early settlement lies hidden under later river mud.
centers.note_zh: 早期的埃及城鎮很難研究：在尼羅河三角洲，早期聚落的證據被後來河水帶來的泥土埋在下面。
centers.src: UNESCO, Memphis and its Necropolis; Harvard University, Digital Giza; Azzazy, PLOS ONE (2018) on the Delta

centers.crops_en: The Indus and its neighbors, fed by the summer monsoon. The cities had straight streets, wells, drains, and bricks of the same sizes.
centers.crops_zh: 印度河和附近的河，靠夏季的季風供水。城市有筆直的街道、水井、排水溝，磚塊的尺寸都一樣。
centers.when_en: The cities flourished from about 2600 BCE (one source says 2500 BCE). Harappa may have held 50,000 people at certain times.
centers.when_zh: 城市大約從西元前 2600 年開始興盛（有一份資料說 2500 年）。哈拉帕在某些時期可能住了五萬人。
centers.note_en: The cities declined slowly after about 1900 BCE. Changing rivers are a leading explanation; there is no evidence that invaders destroyed them.
centers.note_zh: 大約西元前 1900 年以後，這些城市慢慢衰落。河流的改變是主要的解釋之一；並沒有證據顯示它們是被入侵者毀掉的。
centers.src: Kenoyer, harappa.com; UNESCO, Moenjodaro; Giosan et al., PNAS (2012)

centers.crops_en: The Yellow River valley, where millet had been farmed for thousands of years. Erlitou had palaces and bronze workshops.
centers.crops_zh: 黃河流域，那裡種小米已經好幾千年。二里頭有宮殿和鑄造青銅的作坊。
centers.when_en: Early in the second millennium BCE. The later Shang capital at Anyang dates from about 1300 BCE.
centers.when_zh: 西元前第二個千年的早期。後來商朝在安陽的都城，大約從西元前 1300 年開始。
centers.note_en: Whether Erlitou was the capital of the Xia dynasty in the old histories is still argued over.
centers.note_zh: 二里頭是不是古書裡夏朝的都城，到現在還在爭論。
centers.src: Allan, Journal of Asian Studies (2007); UNESCO, Yin Xu

centers.crops_en: The lower Yangtze, a land of rice paddies and wetlands. Liangzhu built a large system of dams and channels around its walled city.
centers.crops_zh: 長江下游，到處是稻田和濕地。良渚在有城牆的城市外圍，建了一大套水壩和水道。
centers.when_zh: 大約西元前 3300 到 2300 年。
centers.note_en: It is not on the Yellow River, which shows that early China had more than one center.
centers.note_zh: 它不在黃河邊，這說明早期的中國不只一個中心。
centers.src: UNESCO, Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City

centers.crops_en: The small Supe River, flowing through a coastal desert. The city stood on a dry terrace above the green valley.
centers.crops_zh: 小小的蘇佩河，流過海岸邊的沙漠。城市蓋在綠色河谷上方一塊乾燥的台地上。
centers.when_en: Between about 3000 and 1800 BCE, according to UNESCO.
centers.when_zh: 依聯合國教科文組織，大約在西元前 3000 到 1800 年之間。
centers.note_en: UNESCO calls it the oldest center of civilization in the Americas, and it was not one of the “four.”
centers.note_zh: 聯合國教科文組織稱它是美洲最古老的文明中心，而它並不在「四大」裡面。

needs.lead_en: A river gave a city some things it needed, and some trouble too. Sort each card into the right basket. There is no timer.
needs.lead_zh: 一條河帶給城市它需要的東西，也帶來麻煩。把每一張卡放進對的籃子。不計時。
needs.ask_en: What does this card show the river doing?
needs.ask_zh: 這張卡裡的河在做什麼？

items.en: Every summer the Nile rose and left fresh mud on the fields.
items.zh: 尼羅河每年夏天漲水，在田裡留下新的泥土。
items.why_en: The new mud refreshed the soil, and the water soaked the fields for the next crop.
items.why_zh: 新的泥土讓地力恢復，水也把田浸透，準備種下一季。
items.hint_en: What do crops need?
items.hint_zh: 農作物需要什麼？

items.en: Boats carried blocks of fine white limestone down the Nile to Giza.
items.zh: 船沿著尼羅河，把一塊塊細白的石灰岩運到吉薩。
items.why_en: A papyrus diary kept by an official named Merer records trips like these for the Great Pyramid.
items.why_zh: 一位叫梅勒的官員留下的莎草紙日誌，記下了為大金字塔做的這種航程。
items.hint_en: How do you move a heavy stone a long way?
items.hint_zh: 重重的石頭要怎麼搬到很遠的地方？

items.en: Over the centuries the floods of the Indus rivers, and the monsoon rains that fed them, grew weaker.
items.zh: 幾百年下來，印度河一帶的洪水，以及供水給它們的季風雨，都慢慢變弱了。
items.why_en: Changing river flows disrupted farming and are a leading explanation for why the Indus cities slowly declined.
items.why_zh: 河水流量的改變打亂了農業，是印度河的城市慢慢衰落的主要解釋之一。
items.hint_en: Does a river always carry the same amount of water?
items.hint_zh: 河的水量永遠都一樣嗎？

items.en: In southern Mesopotamia almost no rain fell, so farmers led river water to their fields.
items.zh: 美索不達米亞南部幾乎不下雨，農夫就把河水引到田裡。
items.why_en: Without the river there would have been no crops at all in this dry land.
items.why_zh: 在這片乾燥的土地上，沒有河就完全種不出東西。
items.hint_en: Where does the water come from if not from the sky?
items.hint_zh: 水不是從天上來，那是從哪裡來？

items.en: In Mesopotamia the floods came at the wrong time for the farming year.
items.zh: 在美索不達米亞，洪水來的時間跟種田的季節對不上。
items.why_en: A recent study points out that, unlike in Egypt and the Indus, the river's high water did not line up with the crops, which made farming harder to organize.
items.why_zh: 一項新的研究指出，和埃及、印度河不同，這裡漲水的時間跟作物的季節對不上，種田因此更難安排。
items.hint_en: Is a flood helpful if it comes at the wrong time?
items.hint_zh: 洪水如果來錯時間，還有幫助嗎？

items.en: Seals carved with Indus signs have been found in Mesopotamia, at cities such as Ur and Kish.
items.zh: 在美索不達米亞的烏爾、基什等城市，挖到了刻著印度河文字符號的印章。
items.why_en: Rivers led to the sea, and the sea linked the cities in trade. Many objects made in the Indus region have turned up in Mesopotamia.
items.why_zh: 河通到海，海又把這些城市用貿易連了起來。在美索不達米亞找到了許多印度河一帶做的東西。
items.hint_en: How did the seal get so far from home?
items.hint_zh: 印章怎麼跑到那麼遠的地方？

items.en: Around 1920 BCE an earthquake blocked the upper Yellow River with a landslide, and when the dam broke, a huge flood rushed downstream.
items.zh: 大約西元前 1920 年，一場地震引發山崩，堵住了黃河上游；堰塞壩潰決時，大洪水往下游沖去。
items.why_en: The flood is well dated. The scientists who studied it link it to the old story of Yu taming the waters; whether it really is that story is debated.
items.why_zh: 這場洪水的年代很清楚。研究它的科學家把它和「大禹治水」的古老故事連在一起；它是不是就是那個故事，還有爭論。
items.hint_en: Is a huge flood good news?
items.hint_zh: 大洪水是好消息嗎？

items.en: At Liangzhu, dams and channels held water for the rice paddies.
items.zh: 在良渚，水壩和水道把水留下來給稻田用。
items.why_en: Rice grows standing in water, so controlling water meant controlling the harvest.
items.why_zh: 稻子是泡在水裡長的，管住了水，就管住了收成。
items.hint_en: What kind of field needs to stand in water?
items.hint_zh: 哪一種田需要泡在水裡？

needs.end_en: A river was never only a gift. Cities beside rivers had to plan for floods, droughts, and rivers that moved. Learning to manage the river was part of what made a city.
needs.end_zh: 河從來不只是禮物。河邊的城市得準備對付洪水、乾旱，還有會搬家的河。學會管理河流，就是城市之所以成為城市的一部分。

timeline.zh: 城市一條線一條線地出現
timeline.lead_en: Each bar marks early cities or large centers in a region. Notice how they overlap, and how many lanes have one. Press “Whole span” to see how recent all of this is.
timeline.lead_zh: 每一條長條標出一個地區早期的城市或大型中心。注意它們怎麼重疊，有幾條線上有。按「全部」看看，這些事其實有多近。
timeline.idle_en: Click a bar or a diamond to read its dates.
timeline.idle_zh: 點一條長條或一個菱形，讀出它的年代。

tips.en: Bars in different lanes that overlap show that cities began in several places at about the same time, not in one place first and then everywhere else.
tips.zh: 不同線上重疊的長條說明：城市差不多同時在好幾個地方開始，不是先在一個地方、再傳到各地。

tips.en: A striped bar marks a date, or an identification, that researchers still debate.
tips.zh: 有條紋的長條，是研究者還在爭論的年代或認定。

tips.en: The gray diamond marks the Great Pyramid, a single project rather than a span of time.
tips.zh: 灰色的菱形標的是大金字塔：它是一件工程，不是一段時間。

events.zh: 美索不達米亞的烏魯克時期
events.note_en: Uruk grows into a city of at least 25,000 people on the marshy delta of the Euphrates and Tigris.
events.note_zh: 烏魯克在幼發拉底河和底格里斯河的沼澤三角洲上，長成至少兩萬五千人的城市。

events.note_en: A walled city with a large system of dams and channels.
events.note_zh: 有城牆的城市，外圍有一大套水壩和水道。

events.note_en: Traditionally about 3000 BCE, as the capital of a unified Egypt; dates for unification vary.
events.note_zh: 傳統的說法是大約西元前 3000 年，做為統一後的埃及的首都；統一的年代有不同的說法。

events.zh: 祕魯蘇佩河谷的卡拉爾
events.note_en: The oldest center of civilization in the Americas, according to UNESCO.
events.note_zh: 聯合國教科文組織說，它是美洲最古老的文明中心。

events.note_en: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro at their height; one source gives 2500 to 1500 BCE for the civilization as a whole.
events.note_zh: 哈拉帕和摩亨約達羅的全盛時期；有一份資料把整個文明定在西元前 2500 到 1500 年。

events.note_en: Built in the reign of Khufu; scholars' dates for his reign differ by decades, and most fall between 2700 and 2500 BCE.
events.note_zh: 在胡夫在位時蓋成；學者們對他在位年代的看法相差幾十年，大多落在西元前 2700 到 2500 年之間。

events.note_en: A center with palaces and bronze workshops. Whether it was the Xia capital is debated.
events.note_zh: 有宮殿和青銅作坊的中心。是不是夏朝的都城還有爭論。

events.note_en: The city of the oracle bones in Lesson 3. A ditch around it also helped control floods.
events.note_zh: 第三課甲骨文的那座城。城外的壕溝也有防洪的作用。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.en: Buried towns, river mud, and a boatman's diary
how_we_know.zh: 埋起來的城鎮、河底的泥，和一位船隊隊長的日誌
how_we_know.lead_en: The first cities left walls, streets, and rubbish behind. The rivers that fed them left clues too.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 最早的城市留下了牆、街道和垃圾。養活它們的河，也留下了線索。

items.en: The workers' town
items.limit_en: The town shows how workers lived, but not exactly how they were recruited. Researchers still debate how much was paid work and how much was a duty owed to the state.
items.limit_zh: 這座城鎮讓我們看到工人怎麼生活，但看不出他們確切是怎麼被找來的。有多少是領酬勞的工作、有多少是對國家的義務，研究者還在討論。
items.src: Ancient Egypt Research Associates; National Geographic History (2017)
items.text_en: Near the pyramids, archaeologists have dug up the town that housed the builders of the Giza pyramids (probably including Khufu's), with workshops, bakeries, storerooms, and officials' houses. The workers' cemetery was found in 1990.
items.text_zh: 在金字塔附近，考古學家挖出了吉薩金字塔建造者住的城鎮（很可能也包括蓋胡夫金字塔的人），有作坊、麵包坊、倉庫，和官員的房子。工人的墓地是 1990 年發現的。

items.en: The diary of Merer
items.limit_en: Merer tells us how stone traveled, not how it was lifted. The logbook says nothing about ramps.
items.limit_zh: 梅勒告訴我們石頭怎麼運來，卻沒說怎麼抬上去。日誌裡沒有提到坡道。
items.src: Tallet and Marouard, Near Eastern Archaeology 77 (2014); Tallet, Les papyrus de la mer Rouge I (IFAO, 2017)
items.text_en: In 2013, papyri were found at an ancient harbor on the Red Sea. They are the logbook of an official named Merer, whose team carried limestone by boat from the quarries at Tura to the Great Pyramid while it was being built. They are the oldest inscribed papyri yet found in Egypt.
items.text_zh: 2013 年，在紅海邊一座古代港口找到了一批莎草紙。它們是一位叫梅勒的官員的工作日誌：大金字塔施工的時候，他的隊伍用船把石灰岩從圖拉的採石場運到工地。這是目前在埃及找到最古老、寫了字的莎草紙。

items.en: Rivers that moved
items.limit_en: Dating old river channels is hard, and linking a change in a river to a change in people's lives is an interpretation, not a direct observation.
items.limit_zh: 古河道很難定年；把河的改變和人的生活改變連在一起，是一種解讀，不是直接看到的事。
items.src: Ghoneim et al., Communications Earth & Environment (2024); Giosan et al., PNAS (2012)
items.text_en: Rivers leave traces. Satellite images and drill cores show an old branch of the Nile, now dried up, that once ran close to the pyramids. Studies of old river beds in the Indus region show how its floods weakened over time.
items.text_zh: 河會留下痕跡。衛星影像和鑽探取出的土芯顯示，有一條現在已經乾掉的尼羅河古支流，以前離金字塔很近。對印度河一帶古河床的研究，讓我們看到它的洪水怎麼隨時間變弱。

views.en: Four questions about rivers and cities
views.zh: 關於河與城市的四個問題
views.lead_en: The questions below have been argued over for a long time. The views are set side by side; this lesson does not choose between them.
views.lead_zh: 下面這些問題已經爭論很久了。各種說法並列，這一課不替誰下結論。
views.rule_en: Notice how often a new kind of evidence, such as river mud or a satellite image, changes the question rather than ending it.
views.rule_zh: 留意新的證據（例如河底的泥或衛星影像）有多常改變問題本身，而不是結束討論。

items.topic_en: Did managing water create the first states?
items.topic_zh: 是管水的需要，造出了最早的國家嗎？

sides.en: The historian Karl Wittfogel argued in 1957 that large irrigation works needed strong central rulers, and that this was how powerful states arose in river valleys.
sides.zh: 歷史學家魏復古（Karl Wittfogel）在 1957 年主張，大型的灌溉工程需要強大的中央統治者，大河流域的強大國家就是這樣出現的。
sides.src: Wittfogel, Oriental Despotism (1957); see “Oriental Despotism”

sides.en: Later researchers found that in Mesopotamia large-scale irrigation is clearly attested only from about 2500 BCE, long after the first cities. A 2025 study suggests that the tides on the delta helped water the earliest fields.
sides.zh: 後來的研究者發現，在美索不達米亞，大規模灌溉要到大約西元前 2500 年才有明確的證據，比最早的城市晚了很多。2025 年的一項研究認為，三角洲上的潮水幫最早的田灌了溉。
sides.src: Giosan and Goodman, PLOS ONE (2025)

items.note_en: Water mattered everywhere, but the order of events differs from place to place.
items.note_zh: 水在每個地方都重要，但事情發生的先後，每個地方不一樣。

items.topic_en: Are there “four great ancient civilizations”?
items.topic_zh: 真的有「四大文明古國」嗎？

sides.en: In 1900 Liang Qichao wrote of four ancient homelands of civilization and tied them to great rivers. Lists like this help students compare a few well-studied places.
sides.zh: 1900 年，梁啟超寫到地球上古代的「文明祖國有四」，並把它們和大河連在一起。像這樣的清單，可以幫學生比較幾個研究得比較多的地方。
sides.src: 梁啟超〈二十世紀太平洋歌〉(1900)

sides.en: Liangzhu on the Yangtze and Caral in Peru were early and complex, and the Olmec of Mexico followed a little later, about 1200 to 500 BCE, yet none is on the list. Even Liang's own four were China, India, Egypt, and Asia Minor, not quite today's version.
sides.zh: 長江的良渚、祕魯的卡拉爾都很早、也很複雜，墨西哥的奧爾梅克稍晚一些（大約西元前 1200 到 500 年），卻都不在清單上。就連梁啟超自己列的四個，也是中國、印度、埃及和小亞細亞，跟今天的版本並不完全一樣。
sides.src: UNESCO, Liangzhu and Caral-Supe; National Geographic Education, “Olmec Civilization”

items.note_en: The number four is a teaching habit, not a discovery.
items.note_zh: 「四」是一種教學習慣，不是一項發現。

items.topic_en: Who built the pyramids?
items.topic_zh: 金字塔是誰蓋的？

sides.en: The Greek writer Herodotus, about 2,000 years after the pyramids were built, claimed they were built by forced labor, and the idea lasted into modern times.
sides.zh: 希臘作家希羅多德在金字塔蓋好大約兩千年之後，說它們是用強迫的勞力蓋的；這個想法一直流傳到現代。
sides.src: National Geographic History (2017)

sides.en: The workers' town and cemetery show Egyptian workers who were fed and cared for. Some researchers stress that they were paid in food; others suggest that many were called up in rotating teams from their home districts.
sides.zh: 工人的城鎮和墓地顯示，蓋金字塔的是有人供應食物、照顧的埃及工人。有些研究者強調他們領的是食物；也有研究者認為，很多人是從家鄉輪班被徵調來的。
sides.src: Harvard University, Digital Giza; Ancient Egypt Research Associates

items.note_en: The evidence rules out the slave story but still leaves room to discuss how free the workers were.
items.note_zh: 證據排除了「奴隸蓋的」這個故事，但工人有多自由，還有討論的空間。

items.topic_en: Why did the Indus cities decline?
items.topic_zh: 印度河的城市為什麼衰落？

sides.en: Early in the 20th century some scholars thought newcomers had conquered the cities. As early as 1964, an archaeologist writing for the Penn Museum disputed this.
sides.zh: 二十世紀初，有些學者認為是外來的人征服了這些城市。早在 1964 年，就有一位為賓州大學博物館撰文的考古學家反駁這種說法。
sides.src: Dales, “The Mythical Massacre at Mohenjo-Daro,” Expedition 6 (1964)

sides.en: Today researchers point to changing river flows and weakening floods and monsoon rains, which disrupted farming. One study argues that weaker floods first encouraged cities, and that as the monsoon kept weakening, settlements shrank.
sides.zh: 今天的研究者指出，河水的流量改變、洪水和季風雨變弱，打亂了農業。有一項研究認為，洪水變弱一開始促成了城市；後來季風繼續變弱，聚落就縮小了。
sides.src: Giosan et al., PNAS (2012); Kenoyer, harappa.com

items.note_en: The decline was slow and differed from region to region, and its causes are still debated.
items.note_zh: 衰落是慢慢發生的，各地區也不一樣，原因到現在還有爭論。

phrases.zh: 比較不同地方的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: Historians compare places without ranking them: what was alike, what was different, and what we still do not know. Listen, repeat, then make your own sentence with the words in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 歷史學家比較不同的地方，但不替它們排名：哪裡一樣、哪裡不一樣、還有什麼不知道。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用粗體的字自己造一句。

rows.en: Both Egypt and Mesopotamia grew up beside great rivers.
rows.html: Both Egypt and Mesopotamia grew up beside great rivers.
rows.zh: 埃及和美索不達米亞都在大河旁邊發展起來。
rows.note_en: both … and …: two things that are alike

rows.en: The Nile rose at about the same time every year, whereas Mesopotamia's floods came at the wrong time for the crops.
rows.html: The Nile rose at about the same time every year, whereas Mesopotamia's floods came at the wrong time for the crops.
rows.zh: 尼羅河每年差不多同一個時候漲水，而美索不達米亞的洪水卻在作物不需要的時候來。
rows.note_en: whereas: sets two different things side by side

rows.en: Unlike the farmers of the Yellow River, the people of Liangzhu grew rice.
rows.html: Unlike the farmers of the Yellow River, the people of Liangzhu grew rice.
rows.zh: 和黃河邊的農夫不同，良渚的人種的是稻米。
rows.note_en: unlike: different from

rows.en: The streets of Harappa were similar to those of Mohenjo-daro.
rows.html: The streets of Harappa were similar to those of Mohenjo-daro.
rows.zh: 哈拉帕的街道和摩亨約達羅的很像。
rows.note_en: similar to: almost the same as

rows.en: A food surplus made it possible for some people not to farm.
rows.html: A food surplus made it possible for some people not to farm.
rows.zh: 多出來的糧食，讓一些人可以不種田。
rows.note_en: made it possible for + person + to: allowed

rows.en: No one knows for certain how the blocks were raised.
rows.html: No one knows for certain how the blocks were raised.
rows.zh: 沒有人能確定石塊是怎麼運上去的。
rows.note_en: no one knows for certain: it is still unknown

rows.en: Changing river flows may have led to the decline of the Indus cities.
rows.html: Changing river flows may have led to the decline of the Indus cities.
rows.zh: 河水流量的改變，可能導致了印度河城市的衰落。
rows.note_en: may have led to: possibly caused

rows.en: Rivers made cities possible, but not certain.
rows.html: Rivers made cities possible, but not certain.
rows.zh: 河讓城市成為可能，卻不保證一定會有。
rows.note_en: possible, but not certain: a condition, not a cause

taiwan_then.eyebrow: Taiwan at That Time · 那時候的台灣
taiwan_then.en: Villages by rivers and the sea
taiwan_then.lead_en: While Uruk and Memphis were growing, people in Taiwan lived in villages near rivers, estuaries, and the coast. There were no cities, but there were farms, fishing, and, later, a very large settlement at Beinan.
taiwan_then.lead_zh: 烏魯克和孟斐斯在長大的時候，台灣的人住在河邊、河口和海邊的村落。那時沒有城市，但有農田、有漁獵，後來還有卑南一處很大的聚落。
taiwan_then.intro_en: Archaeologists in Taiwan usually give dates as “years ago” (before 1950), not as BCE. About 5,000 years ago is roughly 3000 BCE, and 3,500 years ago is roughly 1550 BCE.
taiwan_then.intro_zh: 台灣的考古學家通常用「距今幾年」（以 1950 年為準）來說年代，不用西元前。距今大約 5,000 年，差不多是西元前 3000 年；距今 3,500 年，差不多是西元前 1550 年。

facts.en: The National Museum of Prehistory dates the Dapenkeng culture to between a little over 6,000 and 5,000 years ago. Its sites lie mostly on coasts, at river mouths, and by lakes. Many scholars think these people may be among the earliest ancestors of the Austronesian peoples.
facts.zh: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館把大坌坑文化定在「大約在六千多年前到五千年前之間」。它的遺址大多在海邊、河口和湖邊。許多學者認為，他們可能是南島語族最早的祖先之一。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: In the cord-marked red pottery cultures, about 4,500 to 3,500 years ago, the same museum says life was based mainly on grain farming, while hunting and fishing stayed important.
facts.zh: 在大約距今 4,500 到 3,500 年的細繩紋陶文化，同一座博物館說，生活以穀類農業為主，打獵和捕魚也還是很重要。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: At Beinan in Taitung, on a river terrace beside the Beinan River, people built a village covering more than 50 hectares, with stone buildings, standing stone pillars, and about 1,600 slate coffins. The Beinan culture appeared between about 3,500 and 3,000 years ago and lasted to about 2,300 years ago. It is not the same as today's Puyuma (Beinan) people.
facts.zh: 在台東卑南大溪旁的河階上，人們建了一個面積超過 50 公頃的聚落，有石頭砌的建築、豎立的石柱，還留下大約 1,600 具石板棺。卑南文化大約在距今 3,500 到 3,000 年之間出現，延續到距今 2,300 年前後。它和今天的卑南族並不是同一回事。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館電子報第 360 期；文化部 國家文化記憶庫「卑南考古遺址」

facts.en: A village does not need to become a city. Archaeologists find settled villages of farmers and fishers in Taiwan, but no cities from this time. Why is not known for sure. One idea is that Taiwan's rivers are short and steep, without a wide floodplain like the Nile's, but that is an idea, not a finding.
facts.zh: 村落不一定要變成城市。考古學家在台灣找到許多定居的農耕、漁獵村落，但那個時代沒有找到城市。為什麼，沒有人能確定。有一種想法是：台灣的河又短又陡，沒有尼羅河那樣寬廣的平原；但這只是一種想法，不是發現。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源（定居的聚落）；「河短又陡」是一種可能的解釋，不是研究結論

links.zh: 台灣歷史第二課：幾千年前，誰住在台灣？

links.zh: 台灣歷史第三課：台灣的原住民族是誰？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Evidence · 證據背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A gift, a boatman, a lost wonder count, and a city without pottery
culture_cards.title_zh: 一份禮物、一位船隊隊長、只剩一個的奇觀，和一座沒有陶器的城
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about rivers and the cities beside them.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事，關於河，以及河邊的城市。

cards.body_en: The Greek writer Herodotus, more than 2,000 years after the first pyramids, wrote that much of Egypt was “the gift of the river”: land built up from the mud the Nile carried down. He said the Egyptian priests told him so, and he agreed.
cards.body_zh: 在最早的金字塔出現兩千多年後，希臘作家希羅多德寫道，埃及很多土地是「河的禮物」：是尼羅河帶下來的泥土堆出來的。他說這是埃及的祭司告訴他的，他也同意。

cards.body_en: Merer's team rowed and sailed between the quarries at Tura and Giza, carrying limestone for the Great Pyramid. His logbook, found in 2013 by the Red Sea, records their trips day by day.
cards.body_zh: 梅勒的隊伍在圖拉的採石場和吉薩之間來回划船、揚帆，替大金字塔運石灰岩。他的日誌 2013 年在紅海邊被找到，一天一天地記下了他們的航程。

cards.body_en: Greek writers listed seven wonders of the world. Of those, UNESCO notes, the Great Pyramid of Khufu is the only one that still survives.
cards.body_zh: 希臘人列過世界七大奇觀。聯合國教科文組織指出，其中只有胡夫的大金字塔還留存到今天。

cards.body_en: Caral stands on a dry terrace above the green valley of the Supe River, near the Pacific coast. Its builders raised pyramids and sunken plazas there, and UNESCO calls it the oldest center of civilization in the Americas.
cards.body_zh: 卡拉爾蓋在蘇佩河綠色河谷上方一塊乾燥的台地上，離太平洋海岸不遠。建造它的人在那裡築起金字塔和下沉式廣場；聯合國教科文組織稱它是美洲最古老的文明中心。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (October 2018).
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）。

items.area: 國中・古代文化的遺產
items.area_en: Junior high · the heritage of ancient cultures
items.text: 非洲與西亞的早期文化。
items.note_en: The curriculum suggests focusing on Egypt, and on Sumer, Babylon, and Persia in West Asia, without going into detail. This lesson places Egypt and Mesopotamia beside the other early river cities.
items.note_zh: 課綱建議以埃及，以及西亞的蘇美、巴比倫和波斯為主，不必詳述細節。這一課把埃及和美索不達米亞，和其他早期的河邊城市放在一起看。

items.note_en: The “Taiwan at That Time” card connects to this entry.
items.note_zh: 「那時候的台灣」這張卡對應這個條目。

items.area: 高中・加深加廣選修（科技、環境與藝術的歷史）
items.area_en: Senior high · elective: History of Technology, Environment, and the Arts
items.text: 環境變遷與消失的文明。
items.note_en: The decline of the Indus cities is a case study for this entry.
items.note_zh: 印度河城市的衰落，可以做為這個條目的例子。

myths.myth_en: Slaves built the pyramids.
myths.myth_zh: 金字塔是奴隸蓋的。
myths.fact_en: The workers' town and cemetery show Egyptian workers who were fed with bread and beer. Many may have been called up in rotating teams, but they were not slaves.
myths.fact_zh: 工人的城鎮和墓地顯示，蓋金字塔的是吃麵包、喝啤酒的埃及工人。很多人可能是輪班被徵調來的，但他們不是奴隸。

myths.myth_en: Every pharaoh was buried in a pyramid.
myths.myth_zh: 每一位法老都葬在金字塔裡。
myths.fact_en: Pyramids were the royal tombs of the Old Kingdom and a few later periods. Many later kings were buried in rock-cut tombs in the Valley of the Kings, near Thebes.
myths.fact_zh: 金字塔是古王國和後來少數時期的王陵。很多後來的國王葬在底比斯附近的帝王谷，墓是在岩壁上鑿出來的。

myths.myth_en: There were only four ancient civilizations.
myths.myth_zh: 古代文明只有四個。
myths.fact_en: Liangzhu and Caral were early and complex too, and the Olmec came a little later. “Four” is a teaching habit.
myths.fact_zh: 良渚和卡拉爾也都很早、也很複雜，奧爾梅克稍晚一些。「四」是一種教學習慣。

myths.myth_en: The Indus cities were destroyed suddenly by invaders.
myths.myth_zh: 印度河的城市是被入侵者一下子毀掉的。
myths.fact_en: There is no evidence of an invasion. The cities declined slowly, and changing rivers are a leading explanation.
myths.fact_zh: 沒有入侵的證據。這些城市是慢慢衰落的，河流的改變是主要的解釋之一。

tricks.title_zh: 多出來的糧食，才有城市
tricks.body_en: A city is full of people who do not farm. Someone has to grow their food.
tricks.body_zh: 城市裡滿是不種田的人，總得有人替他們種糧食。

tricks.title_en: Every river has its own temper
tricks.title_zh: 每條河都有自己的脾氣
tricks.body_en: The Nile was regular, Mesopotamia's floods came at the wrong time, the Indus floods weakened.
tricks.body_zh: 尼羅河很規律，美索不達米亞的洪水來錯時間，印度河的洪水變弱了。

tricks.body_en: Add the Yangtze and the Supe. Early cities grew in many places.
tricks.body_zh: 加上長江和蘇佩河。早期的城市長在很多地方。

tricks.body_en: A river gives a chance. People turn it into a city.
tricks.body_zh: 河給了機會，是人把它變成城市。

materials.en: A large sheet of paper and colored pencils for each group
materials.zh: 每組一張大紙和色鉛筆

materials.en: The map from “Where Did the First Cities Grow?”
materials.zh: 「最早的城市長在哪裡？」那張地圖

steps.en: Draw a river crossing your paper. Decide where the high ground is and where the flood reaches.
steps.zh: 在紙上畫一條穿過去的河。決定哪裡是高地，洪水會淹到哪裡。

steps.en: Place the fields, the houses, a granary, a workshop, and a harbor. Explain in English why each goes where it does: “The fields are near the river because…”
steps.zh: 放進田地、房子、穀倉、作坊和碼頭。用英文說明每一樣為什麼放在那裡：「The fields are near the river because…」

steps.en: Your teacher announces a problem: a very high flood, a year with no flood, or the river moving 2 kilometers east. Change your plan.
steps.zh: 老師宣布一個問題：一場超大的洪水、一年沒有氾濫，或是河往東搬了兩公里。修改你們的規劃。

steps.en: Compare plans with another group. Which city would survive best, and why?
steps.zh: 和另一組比較。哪一座城市最能撐下去？為什麼？

activities.tip_en: Step 3 is the lesson. Students see that living by a river means planning for its moods, which is what every early river city had to do.
activities.tip_zh: 第三步就是這堂課的重點。學生會發現，住在河邊就得為它的脾氣做準備，這正是每一座早期的河邊城市都得做的事。

materials.en: About 30 small building blocks or sugar cubes per group
materials.zh: 每組大約 30 個小積木或方糖

materials.en: The 3D model in this lesson
materials.zh: 這一課的 3D 模型

steps.en: Build a stepped pyramid: a bottom layer of 4 × 4 blocks, then 3 × 3, then 2 × 2, then 1. That is 30 blocks.
steps.zh: 蓋一座階梯金字塔：最下層 4 × 4 個，接著 3 × 3、2 × 2，最上面 1 個。一共 30 個。

steps.en: Count how many blocks are in the bottom two layers. Is it more or less than half of 30? (It is 25.)
steps.zh: 數一數最下面兩層有幾個。比 30 的一半多還是少？（是 25 個。）

steps.en: Now open the 3D model and stop at half the height. Compare the gold number with your count.
steps.zh: 接著打開 3D 模型，停在一半的高度，比一比金色的數字和你數的結果。

steps.en: Say it in English: “At half the height, most of the stone is already in place.”
steps.zh: 用英文說：「At half the height, most of the stone is already in place.」

activities.tip_en: This turns a surprising number into something students can hold. The top of a pyramid is small but hard to reach, which is why the ramp question matters.
activities.tip_zh: 這個活動把一個讓人意外的數字變成摸得到的東西。金字塔的頂端很小卻很難到達，這就是坡道的問題重要的原因。

lessons.title: What Did the Greeks Start?
lessons.blurb_en: Watch the people of Attica in 3D and find out how few of them could climb the Pnyx hill to vote. Decide who could vote in Athens, and test two ancient readings of the rule for sending a man away for ten years.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 裡看看阿提卡的居民，發現能走上普尼克斯山投票的人有多少。判斷誰能在雅典投票，再試試「把一個人送走十年」那條規則的兩種古代讀法。
lessons.big_idea_en: From about 508 BCE, the adult male citizens of Athens met in an assembly and decided their city's affairs by voting. In the same age, some Greeks began to look for answers by asking questions and giving reasons. Both were beginnings, not finished things: most people in Athens could not vote, and other peoples also made decisions together.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 大約從西元前 508 年起，雅典的成年男性公民聚在公民大會裡，用投票決定城邦的事。同一個時代，有些希臘人開始用提問和講道理的方式找答案。兩件事都是開頭，不是完成品：住在雅典的大多數人不能投票，而其他民族也有一起做決定的方式。

lab.title_en: Who Could Climb the Pnyx to Vote?
lab.title_zh: 誰能上普尼克斯山投票？
lab.how_en: The plain of Attica holds everyone who lived around Athens, in four groups; each small figure stands for about 100 people. Switch to “Who could vote” and only one group stays lit. Then send the voters to a meeting on the Pnyx hill, and finally hold a show of hands. The numbers are one scholar's estimates for the 300s BCE; other scholars give different figures, listed on the right.
lab.how_zh: 阿提卡平原上是住在雅典周圍的所有人，分成四群；每個小人代表大約 100 人。切換到「誰能投票」，只剩一群亮著。接著讓能投票的人去普尼克斯山開會，最後舉手表決。人數用的是一位學者對西元前 300 年代的估計；其他學者的數字不一樣，列在右邊。

groups.range_en: About 30,000 in the 300s BCE. For 431 BCE, estimates run from about 43,000 (an older estimate based on Thucydides) to at least 60,000 (Hansen)
groups.range_zh: 西元前 300 年代約三萬；西元前 431 年的估計，從約四萬三千（根據修昔底德的舊估計）到至少六萬（漢森）

groups.en: Women and children of citizen families
groups.zh: 公民家庭的女性和孩子
groups.range_zh: 約七萬（全部公民加起來約十萬）

groups.zh: 住在雅典的自由外邦人（外籍居民）

groups.range_en: “As many as 150,000” by one estimate; estimates vary widely
groups.range_zh: 依一個估計「多達十五萬」；各家估計差很多

lab.proposal_en: Proposal: build more warships this year?
lab.proposal_zh: 提案：今年要不要多造幾艘戰船？

yes.en: Clearly more hands up: the proposal passes.
yes.zh: 舉手的明顯比較多：提案通過。

no.en: Clearly fewer hands up: the proposal fails.
no.zh: 舉手的明顯比較少：提案不通過。

close.en: Too close to judge by eye. The presiding officers have to decide, or ask for the vote again.
close.zh: 太接近了，用看的看不出來。得由主持的人決定，或請大家再表決一次。

modes.text_en: Each figure is about 100 people. The biggest group is the enslaved people, by this estimate, and the citizen men are one of the smaller ones.
modes.text_zh: 每個小人約 100 人。照這組估計，最大的一群是被奴役的人，而男性公民是比較小的一群。

modes.text_en: Only adult men whose parents were both citizens could vote. Women, metics, and enslaved people could not, however long they had lived in Attica.
modes.text_zh: 只有父母都是公民的成年男子能投票。女性、外籍居民和被奴役的人都不能，不管他們在阿提卡住了多久。

modes.zh: 普尼克斯山上的一場大會
modes.text_en: The first meeting place on the Pnyx held about 6,000 people. Later rebuildings made it larger, up to about 13,400 if packed tight; the historian Mogens Hansen doubts that so many ever came.
modes.text_zh: 普尼克斯山最早的會場坐得下大約 6,000 人。後來重建，最大一期擠一擠可坐大約 13,400 人；歷史學家漢森懷疑從來沒有那麼多人到過。

modes.text_en: The Assembly usually voted by raising hands, and a simple majority decided. Hands were judged by eye; when the two sides look close, it is hard to tell. The point at which a vote looks “too close” is this model's assumption.
modes.text_zh: 公民大會通常舉手表決，簡單多數決定。舉手是用看的判斷；兩邊看起來很接近的時候，很難分得出來。多接近算「太接近」，是這個模型的假設。

lab.numbers_note_en: The four groups use one estimate for the mid-300s BCE reported by Britannica. Other scholars estimate 250,000 people in all for 431 BCE (Hansen) or 400,000 or more (Akrigg). No census survives, so every number is an estimate.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 四群人用的是大英百科全書引用的一個西元前 300 年代中期的估計。其他學者估計西元前 431 年總共約二十五萬人（漢森），或四十萬以上（阿克里格）。沒有留下任何人口普查，所以每個數字都是估計。

legend.en: Adult male citizens: the only people who could vote
legend.zh: 成年男性公民：唯一能投票的人

legend.en: Everyone else who lived in Attica
legend.zh: 住在阿提卡的其他所有人

legend.en: The Pnyx, where the assembly met
legend.zh: 普尼克斯山，公民大會開會的地方

lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch. Each small figure stands for many people; the groups are drawn side by side to compare their sizes, not where people lived. The hill, the platform, and the Acropolis are simplified, and the distances are not to scale.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意。每個小人代表很多人；四群人並排是為了比大小，不是他們住在哪裡。山坡、講台和衛城都簡化了，距離也不照比例。
lab.credit_html: Model: an illustration made for this lesson. Population estimates and the size of the Pnyx follow the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 模型：為這一課製作的示意。人口估計和普尼克斯山的大小，依本頁最下面列出的資料。

paras: In Lesson 4, rulers and officials organized the first cities. Around 500 BCE, in a small Greek city-state called Athens, people tried something different. In about 508 BCE, a leader named Cleisthenes reorganized the citizens into ten new tribes and a Council of 500, chosen from all over Attica, the land around the city. From then on, the citizens themselves decided many of the city's affairs.

They decided in the Assembly. Three or four times a month, citizens climbed a hill called the Pnyx, listened to speeches from a stone platform, and voted, usually by raising their hands. Any citizen could stand up and speak, for or against a proposal; proposals came first from the Council of 500. The Greeks called this kind of government dēmokratia, “rule by the people.” Many officials were not elected but chosen by lot, so that ordinary citizens took turns holding office.

But who were “the people”? Only adult men whose parents were citizens. Women could not vote. Neither could metics, the free foreigners who lived and worked in Athens, nor the many enslaved people. By one scholar's estimate for the 300s BCE, about 30,000 citizen men lived among roughly 230,000 other people. And the earliest meeting place on the Pnyx that archaeologists can measure held only about 6,000 at a time.

Athenian democracy also had unusual tools. Once a year, the citizens could vote to send away one powerful man for ten years. Each voter scratched a name on a broken piece of pottery called an ostrakon, which is where the word “ostracism” comes from. Archaeologists have found thousands of these ostraka. Democracy did not always last, either: in 411 and again in 404 BCE, small groups seized power for a time, before the citizens restored it.

In the same age, some Greeks began to explain the world with reasons instead of only with stories. Thales is said to have predicted an eclipse in 585 BCE. In Athens, Socrates questioned people about justice and goodness, and he was put on trial and sentenced to death by a jury of citizens in 399 BCE. He wrote nothing himself; we know him mostly from his student Plato.

Greece was not the only place where new ideas were growing. Confucius taught in China, the Buddha taught in India, and the Persian Empire ruled lands from Egypt to Central Asia. Other peoples also made decisions together: a Buddhist text praises the Vajjis of India for meeting frequently and holding many meetings. What Athens started was one beginning among several, and later peoples, including many today, have argued about what it means.
paras_zh: 在第四課，最早的城市是由統治者和官員組織起來的。大約西元前 500 年，在希臘一個叫雅典的小城邦，人們試了一種不一樣的做法。大約西元前 508 年，一位叫克里斯提尼的領袖把公民重新編成十個新的部落，又設了一個從整個阿提卡（雅典城周圍的土地）選出來的五百人議事會。從那時起，城邦的很多事由公民自己決定。
他們在公民大會裡做決定。每個月三、四次，公民爬上一座叫普尼克斯的山丘，聽人站在石頭講台上演說，然後投票，通常是舉手。任何公民都可以站起來發言，支持或反對一項提案；提案要先由五百人議事會提出。希臘人把這種政治叫做 dēmokratia，「由人民統治」。很多官職不是選出來的，而是抽籤決定，讓一般的公民輪流擔任。
但是「人民」是誰？只有父母都是公民的成年男子。女性不能投票。外籍居民（metic）也不能，也就是在雅典生活、工作的自由外邦人；為數眾多的被奴役的人也不能。依一位學者對西元前 300 年代的估計，大約三萬名男性公民，和大約二十三萬個其他的人住在一起。而考古學家能量出來的、普尼克斯山最早的會場，一次只坐得下大約六千人。
雅典的民主還有一些特別的做法。每年一次，公民可以投票，把一位有權勢的人送走十年。每個投票的人在一塊叫 ostrakon 的破陶片上刻一個名字，「陶片放逐」這個詞就是從這裡來的。考古學家找到了好幾千塊這樣的陶片。民主也不是一直都在：西元前 411 年和 404 年，一小群人兩度奪取政權一段時間，後來公民才又把民主恢復。
在同一個時代，有些希臘人開始用道理、而不只是用故事來解釋世界。據說泰利斯在西元前 585 年預測了一次日食。在雅典，蘇格拉底向人追問什麼是正義、什麼是善；西元前 399 年，他被一個由公民組成的陪審團審判，判了死刑。他自己沒有寫下任何東西，我們主要是從他的學生柏拉圖那裡認識他。
長出新想法的地方，不只希臘。孔子在中國教學，佛陀在印度說法，波斯帝國統治著從埃及到中亞的土地。其他民族也有一起做決定的方式：一部佛教經典稱讚印度的跋耆人常常集會、多次集會。雅典開的頭，是好幾個開頭中的一個；後來的人，包括今天的很多人，一直在討論它的意義。
questions: Who could vote in the Athenian Assembly, and who could not?
Why do you think the Athenians chose many officials by lot instead of by election?
The lesson calls Athens “one beginning among several.” What other beginnings does it mention?
answers: Only adult men whose parents were citizens could vote. Women, metics (free foreigners living in Athens), and enslaved people could not.
A lottery gave ordinary citizens, not only rich or famous ones, a turn at holding office. Students may also suggest that it made bribery and campaigning less useful.
Confucius teaching in China, the Buddha teaching in India, the Persian Empire, and the Vajjis of India meeting in assembly.

vocab.ex: Only a citizen could vote in the Assembly.
vocab.exzh: 只有公民能在公民大會投票。

vocab.ex: The word democracy comes from Greek.
vocab.exzh: 「民主」這個字來自希臘文。

vocab.ex: The Assembly met on the Pnyx.
vocab.exzh: 公民大會在普尼克斯山開會。

vocab.ex: They voted by raising their hands.
vocab.exzh: 他們舉手投票。

vocab.ex: The majority decided the result.
vocab.exzh: 由多數決定結果。

vocab.ex: Many officials were chosen by lot.
vocab.exzh: 很多官員是抽籤選出來的。

vocab.ex: Athens was a Greek city-state.
vocab.exzh: 雅典是一個希臘城邦。

vocab.ex: Socrates questioned everyone he met.
vocab.exzh: 蘇格拉底向遇到的每個人追問。
